igeo-2027.about:
The International Geography Olympiad (iGeo), held under the auspices of the International Geographical Union, is an annual competition for the best geography students aged 16 to 19. It has grown from five countries in 1996 to around 50 today. The 2027 iGeo takes place in Jelgava, Latvia, from 2 to 9 August 2027 (future hosts: Melbourne, Australia, in 2028 and Burgas, Bulgaria, in 2029).

The competition has three parts: a written response test (about 40% of marks), a fieldwork exercise in the host region in which students collect data and produce a map and analysis (about 40%), and a multimedia test (about 20%). It also includes a poster presentation and a cultural programme with students from every continent.

Students are chosen from the thousands who take part in their own National Geography Olympiads; each country sends a team of four. iGeo is a distinctive achievement for applications in geography, environmental science, urban planning or international relations, and the fieldwork element is a genuine research experience.
highlights: Jelgava, Latvia, 2–9 August 2027
Written test, fieldwork exercise and multimedia test
Teams of four, aged 16–19
igeo-2027.eligibility: Students aged 16–19 selected through their country's National Geography Olympiad (each country sends up to four). Individual entry is not possible.
how_to_apply: Check the iGeo site ('How to Qualify') for your country's national olympiad contact.
Register for your national geography olympiad through your school.
Prepare with past iGeo tests and fieldwork exercises on geoolympiad.org.
Qualify for the national team of four for iGeo 2027.
igeo-2027.costs: National rounds are usually free. The host provides accommodation and the programme for teams; travel and fees are normally covered by the national organiser.

ieo-2027.about:
The International Economics Olympiad (IEO) is an annual competition for high-school students in economics and finance, supported by Nobel laureate Eric Maskin. It brings together teams from around 74 countries, with more than 600,000 students taking part in national competitions each year. The olympiad includes individual rounds on economics and financial literacy and a team business case, all in English.

Each country is represented by one team of up to five contestants, selected by a long-term national partner (the 'Sending Organization'). Contestants must have been born less than 20 years before 30 June 2027 and be working toward a secondary-school diploma. The IEO 2027 annual regulations have been published; the host and exact dates are still to be announced, and the olympiad normally takes place on site in July or August. The host covers accommodation and full board for contestants and team leaders.

If your country is on the IEO participating-countries list, find the national competition there and enter this school year; if not, the IEO invites organisations to contact it to set up a national selection. It is a strong credential for economics, business and finance applications.
highlights: Teams of up to five; ~74 participating countries
Economics, finance and a team business case
Host covers board and lodging for teams
ieo-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students born less than 20 years before 30 June 2027, selected by their country's IEO partner organisation. One team per country.
how_to_apply: Check the 'Participating Countries' section on ecolymp.org for your national competition.
Register for the national economics olympiad/selection.
Prepare with past IEO tasks and the business case materials.
If selected, travel with your national team to IEO 2027.
ieo-2027.costs: National rounds vary (often free). Host covers accommodation and meals; travel and any participation fee are usually covered by the sending organisation.

iypt-2027.about:
The International Young Physicists' Tournament (IYPT), sometimes called the 'Physics World Cup', is a team competition for secondary-school students. Instead of a timed exam, teams spend months investigating 17 open-ended problems (real phenomena to model, measure and explain), then present and defend their research in 'Physics Fights' where teams take the roles of reporter, opponent and reviewer in front of a jury.

The 40th IYPT will be held in Auckland, New Zealand, from 5 to 12 July 2027. The 17 problems for 2027 were published on 15 July 2026 on iypt.org, so national teams are already working on them. Teams are registered by authorised IYPT member organisations; pre-registration closes on 15 December 2026.

Students usually reach the IYPT through a national young physicists' tournament or selection organised by their country's member organisation. It is excellent preparation for real research, scientific English and argumentation, and is highly regarded by physics and engineering departments.

17 open research problems already published
Teams debate solutions in 'Physics Fights'
iypt-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students on a national team registered by their country's IYPT member organisation (team rules and age limits per the IYPT regulations).
how_to_apply: Read the IYPT 2027 problems on iypt.org and pick ones to investigate.
Find your national tournament or IYPT member organisation (see 'National Tournaments' on iypt.org).
Take part in national selection to join the team.
Your national organiser registers the team (pre-registration closes 15 December 2026).
iypt-2027.costs: Depends on national organiser; the international tournament charges participation fees to teams, usually covered by national organisers or sponsors.

immc-2027.about:
The International Mathematical Modeling Challenge (IM²C) is a team competition for secondary-school students that focuses on mathematical modelling: turning an open, real-world problem (for example scheduling, resource allocation or risk) into mathematics, solving it, testing assumptions and communicating the result in a written report. Unlike olympiads, there is no single right answer; judges reward sound reasoning, creativity and clear writing.

The 2027 IM²C starts on 1 February 2027. Teams (typically up to four students with a faculty advisor) work on the problem during a period of consecutive days within the contest window, at school and with any resources except outside help. The challenge runs through regional and national competitions in 54 countries and regions, whose best reports go forward to international judging; top teams are recognised at the IM²C summit.

It is ideal for students who like applied maths, data, economics or engineering, and the report is an impressive research-style writing sample.

Open real-world modelling problem; team report
Regional organisers in 54 countries and regions
immc-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students in teams with a teacher advisor, entered through their country's or region's IM²C organiser.
how_to_apply: Find your country/region's organiser on immchallenge.org ('Countries & Regions').
Form a team and find a teacher advisor; register with the national organiser.
Practise with past IM²C problems and winning reports.
Choose your consecutive working days in the 2027 window and submit the report.
immc-2027.costs: Free or low-cost depending on the national organiser.

first-global-challenge-2027.about:
The FIRST Global Challenge is an annual international robotics competition, often called the 'Olympics of robotics', in which one team of students aged roughly 14–18 represents each participating country. Teams from more than 190 countries receive the same robot kit and build robots to play a game themed around a global challenge (recent themes include energy, carbon capture, food security and ocean health), competing in cooperative alliances rather than country against country.

FIRST Global has announced that the 2027 Challenge will be held in Madrid, Spain; the 2026 edition took place on 7–10 October 2026 in the Republic of Korea. Dates, venue and the 2027 theme will be published on first.global.

Each country's team is recruited by a national team organiser (often a ministry, university or STEM non-profit). If you are interested, contact your country's current team via the National Teams pages or FIRST Global's contact form, since recruitment usually starts in the first half of the year.

Robots built from a common kit around a global theme
2027 host: Madrid, Spain
first-global-challenge-2027.eligibility: Students aged about 14–18 selected by their country's FIRST Global national team organiser. Countries without a team can apply to FIRST Global to form one.

first-global-challenge-2027.costs: FIRST Global provides the robot kit; costs for travel are typically covered by national organisers and sponsors.

ukmt-intermediate-mathematical-challenge.about:
The Intermediate Mathematical Challenge (IMC) from the UK Mathematics Trust is a 60-minute, 25-question multiple-choice paper designed to encourage mathematical reasoning, precision of thought and fluency. Questions start accessible and become genuinely challenging, so it suits a wide range of students. It is taken by hundreds of thousands of students each year in UK schools and in overseas schools (for England, Wales and overseas: Year 11 and below).

In 2026–27 the challenge is sat on Wednesday 27 January 2027, on paper. Schools register with UKMT and buy entries: posted papers must be bought by 6 January 2027, downloadable papers by 27 January 2027, and answer sheets uploaded by 28 January 2027. Certificates are awarded, and the highest scorers are invited to the follow-on rounds (Grey and Pink Kangaroo, and the Cayley, Hamilton and Maclaurin Olympiads).

It is a respected, inexpensive way for British-curriculum and other international schools to give students an olympiad pathway, with free past papers and video solutions on the UKMT site.
highlights: Sat in schools worldwide on 27 January 2027
Follow-on Kangaroo and Olympiad rounds for top scorers
Free past papers and video solutions
ukmt-intermediate-mathematical-challenge.eligibility: Students in Year 11 and below (England, Wales and overseas), entered by a registered school. Schools outside the UK can register.

The school buys IMC entries (posted papers by 6 January 2027; downloads by 27 January 2027).

commonwealth-short-story-prize-2027.about:
The Commonwealth Short Story Prize, run by the Commonwealth Foundation, is awarded for the best piece of unpublished short fiction (2,000–5,000 words) in English or translated into English. Stories are judged in five regions (Africa, Asia, Canada and Europe, the Caribbean, and the Pacific); regional winners are published by the literary magazine Granta and the overall winner receives a cash prize. Entries can be submitted in several languages besides English, which makes it unusually accessible.

For 2027, the Foundation has postponed the opening of the prize until January 2027 so it can comprehensively review its processes, entry rules and submission guidelines, including how to respond to AI-generated writing. Full rules and the closing date will be published when entries open.

It is free to enter and is one of the most respected routes to international publication for emerging writers aged 18 and over from Commonwealth countries.

Regional winners published by Granta

commonwealth-short-story-prize-2027.eligibility: Citizens of Commonwealth countries aged 18 and over (check the 2027 rules when published). Unpublished work only.
how_to_apply: Check commonwealthfoundation.com/short-story-prize in January 2027 for the new rules.

advent-of-code-2026.about:
Advent of Code is an advent calendar of small programming puzzles for a variety of skill levels, created by Eric Wastl and running every December since 2015. Each day a new two-part puzzle unlocks; you solve it in any programming language and submit the answer computed from your personal input. Puzzles start gentle and grow harder, touching on parsing, simulation, graphs, dynamic programming and optimisation.

The 2026 event starts on 1 December 2026. It is free (supporters can optionally buy AoC++), needs only a login via an existing account (such as GitHub or Google), and puzzles remain available after December, so you can work through them at your own pace. Schools and clubs can create private leaderboards to compete with each other.

People use Advent of Code as interview preparation, company training, university coursework and speed-coding practice; for school students it is a fun daily habit that builds the problem-solving skills needed for USACO, national olympiads and the CCC.

Any programming language
Private leaderboards for schools and clubs

treehacks-2027.about:
TreeHacks is Stanford University's premier hackathon, run by students. For 36 hours, from 12 to 14 February 2027, on Stanford's campus, hackers form teams to build software and hardware projects that tackle real problems, with workshops, mentors from leading tech companies and sponsor challenges. 2027 is the event's 13th edition.

Any enrolled college student (undergraduate or graduate) from anywhere in the world can apply. Admitted hackers attend for free: TreeHacks covers flights (subject to regional caps), food, swag and designated sleeping spaces, and teams compete for more than USD 1 million in prizes.

It is one of the most selective and well-resourced student hackathons in the world, and a great way to build a project portfolio and meet founders and engineers in Silicon Valley.

Infinity MUN ('Where Future Diplomats Become Global Leaders') is a student-built conference in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. With only 160 delegate seats across eight committees, rooms stay small enough for every delegate to speak often, which suits beginners as well as experienced MUNers.

The conference runs 26–28 November 2026 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia and is aimed at high school and university students. Working language: English. Committees: 8 committees with 20 delegate seats each (agendas to be revealed).

Apply as a delegate or chair through the forms linked on the official site; accepted delegates receive a confirmation and a welcome packet. Position papers can be submitted up to the day before the conference. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.

limun-uc-2027.about:
The London International Model United Nations University Conference brings chairs, ambassadors and delegates from all over the world to London each February. The 2027 edition asks delegates how diplomacy can balance national interest with a stable, cooperative international order. LIMUN is run by the LIMUN Foundation, a UK charity that also runs a high-school conference and scholarship programmes.

The conference runs 19–21 February 2027 in London, United Kingdom at Opening ceremony at Central Hall Westminster; committee sessions at King's College London and is aimed at university students. Working language: English. Committees: General Assembly, ECOSOC, Security Council, specialised agencies and crisis committees (allocations in the portal).

Individuals and university societies apply through the Delegate Portal (head delegates or faculty advisors register a group first). LIMUN offers scholarship programmes for delegates who could not otherwise attend; socials such as the Ball are ticketed separately. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.

Its 2027 committees are the General Assembly, the Security Council and UNDP, with topics ranging from AI in international security to climate adaptation. Because everyone stays at the conference venue, it has a close, community feel and is popular with first-timers.

The conference runs 18–21 February 2027 in Berlin, Germany at DJH Jugendherberge Berlin-Am Wannsee (accommodation and sessions at the same venue) and is aimed at university students. Working language: English. Committees: General Assembly (sustainable tourism; rural poverty), Security Council (AI and international security; Haiti), UNDP (resilience to crises; climate adaptation).

bayernmun-2027.about:
BayernMUN is hosted by the United Nations Society Nuremberg, in the 'city of human rights'. The 2027 edition is its largest yet, with five councils (including a NATO council) and a press team, and committee agendas linked to the Sustainable Development Goals.

The conference runs 22–24 January 2027 in Nuremberg, Germany at Imperial Castle Nuremberg (Kaiserburg) and is aimed at high school and university students. Working language: English. Committees: Five councils including a NATO council, plus a press team.

Register and pay through the official registration page, then complete your personal information. Scholarships that refund ticket fees are available, and the organisers issue invitation letters for visa applications. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.

MainMUN is one of Germany's established student-run Model UN conferences, organised with the MainMUN Foundation and Goethe University Frankfurt. Its committees are labelled by level (beginner to expert) and it runs press agencies modelled on BBC World News, Xinhua and PanaPress.

nmun-ny-2027.about:
National Model United Nations has run since 1927 and is often called the original Model UN. NMUN•NY takes place in two sessions (NY-A 21–25 March and NY-B 29 March–2 April 2027) at the New York Hilton Midtown, with closing events at the United Nations when available. Universities usually attend as a delegation representing one country or NGO.

The conference runs 21–25 March 2027 in New York, United States at New York Hilton Midtown (with sessions at UN Headquarters, subject to UN approval) and is aimed at university students. Working language: English. Committees: General Assembly committees, ECOSOC bodies, Security Council, specialised agencies and NGO delegations.

Faculty advisors register the university delegation, receive a country/NGO assignment, confirm numbers and hotel rooms, and submit position papers by 1 March 2027. Many universities fund NMUN travel through academic courses. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.

amun-chicago-2026.about:
American Model United Nations has run for decades as a university-level simulation focused on realistic UN practice. Besides General Assembly and Security Council simulations, it offers an International Court of Justice, a Commission of Inquiry and an International Press Delegation, each with its own registration.

The conference runs 21–24 November 2026 in Chicago, United States at Sheraton Grand Chicago Riverwalk and is aimed at university students. Working language: English. Committees: General Assembly, Security Council, historical Security Council, International Court of Justice, Commission of Inquiry, International Press Delegation and other UN bodies.

A school reserves each country with a non-refundable US$120 deposit and then fills in a country-selection form; individuals can also register. AMUN offers scholarships and free training toolkits. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.

namun-2027.about:
North American Model United Nations is hosted at the University of Toronto and is one of Canada's longest-running university MUNs, celebrating 42 years in 2027. Committees range from large General Assemblies to fast-paced crisis rooms, and position-paper awards are given.

web-summit-qatar-2027-volunteers.about:
Web Summit Qatar is the Middle East edition of Web Summit, the global technology conference, held in Doha with the support of Qatar's government. The 2027 edition runs from 31 January to 3 February 2027 and brings together tens of thousands of attendees, thousands of startups, investors and speakers from across the tech industry.

The volunteer programme recruits people to help run the event: guiding attendees, supporting stages and startup areas, registration and logistics. In return volunteers receive a free ticket to Web Summit Qatar 2027, behind-the-scenes experience of a world-class event, and the chance to network with founders, investors and other volunteers.

For university students interested in technology, entrepreneurship, media or event management, it is the cheapest way to access a conference whose regular tickets cost hundreds of dollars, and a strong addition to a CV.

moehe-national-scientific-research-innov.about:
The National Competition for Scientific Research and Innovation is the Ministry of Education and Higher Education's flagship research competition for schools in Qatar, culminating in the National Scientific Research and Innovation Exhibition (the 2026 exhibition hosted more than 2,900 students). It has a Design for Change track for primary schools and a research track for preparatory and secondary students.

In the research track, students work alone or in pairs under a school supervisor on a 15–25 page project in one of nine science categories. Projects go through school-level exhibitions, plagiarism checks, electronic judging and a final presentation round before the national exhibition. Projects involving human subjects, vertebrate animals or hazardous agents need prior school ethics approval. Government schools take part automatically and private and international schools may opt in.

The top six projects represent Qatar at the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) in the United States, the world's largest pre-college science fair, and selected projects from grades 9–12 also go to ITEX in Malaysia and the Kuwait innovation exhibition for girls. It is the main route for school students in Qatar to an international science-fair stage.

Top six projects go to ISEF in the USA
Also selects teams for ITEX Malaysia and Kuwait
moehe-national-scientific-research-innov.eligibility: Preparatory and secondary students at government schools in Qatar (mandatory) and at private or international schools that opt in. In pair projects, one student must be Qatari unless the school is exempt (e.g., international schools).

Advance through electronic judging and the final round to the national exhibition
moehe-national-scientific-research-innov.costs: Free; travel to ISEF and other international fairs is organised for selected students.

wcmq-healing-hands-essay-competition-202.about:
The Healing Hands Essay Competition is Weill Cornell Medicine-Qatar's annual writing contest for Qatari high school students who are curious about medicine. Each year WCM-Q announces a different medical theme, and students write an original English essay sharing their views on a pressing health issue and proposing creative solutions.

Winners receive the Qatar Doctor of the Future Scholarship: a fully funded two-week visit to Weill Cornell Medicine in New York City, with visits to leading research laboratories and time with Weill Cornell researchers in major New York hospitals. Travel costs are covered for the winner and one escorting parent. Winning essays and ten finalists receive honourable mentions at a reception hosted by the WCM-Q dean. Past winners were mostly in grades 10 and 11.

For Qatari students considering medicine, it is a rare chance to experience an Ivy League medical centre first-hand and a distinctive achievement for future applications to WCM-Q or other medical schools.

qf-academic-bridge-program-2027.about:
The Academic Bridge Program (ABP), founded in 2001 as a Qatar Foundation centre in Education City, admits secondary school graduates from Qatar and the region who need to strengthen their English, mathematics and science to get into, and succeed at, highly selective universities. More than 4,500 students have graduated, many continuing to Education City branch campuses such as Georgetown, Carnegie Mellon, Texas A&M and Weill Cornell, or universities abroad.

Students follow one of three tracks (STEM, Social Sciences, or Humanities and Visual Arts) with courses in academic English, maths, sciences, computer science and social entrepreneurship, plus IELTS preparation, academic advising and a Gateway to University programme that includes cross-registration in Education City. ABP is accredited by the Commission on English Language Program Accreditation (CEA) and by WASC.

Applicants need a high school certificate with an average of 70% or above (lower averages can be reviewed) and IELTS 4.5 or equivalent (TOEFL or Duolingo accepted). Tuition is QR 80,000 per year, but Qatari students are commonly sponsored by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education or employers. ABP also hosts events such as Harvard Model Congress Middle East.

STEM, Social Sciences or Humanities tracks
Strong pathway into Education City universities

york-presidents-international-scholarshi.about:
The President's International Scholarship of Excellence (PISE) is York University's most valuable award for international high-school students starting a bachelor's degree in Toronto. It is worth C$45,000 a year, renewable for four years (C$180,000 in total), which covers most or all of international tuition depending on the programme. PISE recipients also join a scholars' community with mentors, career support and networking with senior faculty; recent winners come from India, Pakistan, the UAE, Kenya, Mongolia, Nigeria and many other countries.

You must be a high-school student entering the first year of a York undergraduate degree in Fall 2027 with a final admission average of at least 80% (A) or equivalent, and be officially nominated by your guidance counsellor, principal or another senior school official. Each school can nominate at most two students. Selection looks at academic excellence, volunteer work, extracurricular activities and leadership. The award cannot be combined with York's automatic entrance scholarships.

First apply to York for admission, then submit the online International Scholarship Application (with your top achievements and essay) by 27 January 2027. York then emails your nominator, who must submit the nomination form and reference letter by 4 February 2027.

Open to international high-school students of any country
School nomination required (max two per school)

mcgill-major-entrance-scholarships-2027.about:
McGill University in Montreal, Canada's top-ranked university in many global tables, offers centrally administered entrance scholarships to first-time university students. Major Entrance Scholarships are worth C$3,000, C$5,000, C$10,000 or C$12,000 a year, renewable for up to four years (total C$12,000–48,000); the C$12,000 level is only for Canadian citizens and permanent residents, so international students can receive up to C$10,000 a year (C$40,000 in total).

Selection committees award them on academic achievement and outstanding leadership in school or community activities. Every applicant to an eligible programme is also automatically considered for a one-year C$3,000 entrance scholarship. Some programmes (e.g. certain professional ones) are excluded.

Applications open on 1 October in McGill's Undergraduate Admissions applicant portal. Students at schools outside Canada must apply for admission by 15 January 2027 and submit the Major Entrance Scholarship application, with two reference letters and a signed school statement if available, by 21 January 2027 (midnight Montreal time).

Leadership counts alongside grades

nyu-abu-dhabi-financial-aid-2027.about:
NYU Abu Dhabi is a highly selective liberal arts and sciences campus of New York University on Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi, where students earn an NYU degree and spend semesters at NYU's global sites. Admission is through the Common App, followed by an invitation-only Candidate Weekend.

For students who are not UAE nationals, all financial aid offered by NYUAD is based on financial need, calculated by NYU's Office of Financial Aid from the CSS Profile. Award amounts vary with each family's need and can cover a large part or all of the cost of attendance; aid is normally renewed at the same level each year if renewal requirements are met. (Emirati students receive the separate Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Scholarship.)

Apply by 1 November 2026 (ED I), 1 January 2027 (ED II) or 5 January 2027 (Regular Decision), and file the CSS Profile by 10 November, 10 January or 1 February respectively, before decisions are released. Missing the CSS deadline can cost you aid.

Aid renewed annually at the same level
NYU degree with study at NYU's global sites

aus-presidents-scholarship-2027.about:
The American University of Sharjah (AUS) is one of the leading US-style universities in the Gulf, accredited in the US and known for engineering, architecture, business and the arts. Its President's Scholarship is aimed at outstanding applicants who completed their secondary education outside the UAE, and covers 100% of tuition and lab fees plus an application-fee waiver for the length of the degree (subject to continuation conditions).

The academic bar is very high: a 98% cumulative average in grades 10 and 11 and 98% in grade 12 (or the equivalent in other systems), a high IELTS/English score, and either three AP exams at grade 5 or an SAT composite of at least 1400 (predicted APs or SAT submitted with the admission application). Students who do not qualify can still be considered for AUS merit scholarships (10–20% of tuition) and need-based grants.

You must first receive an admission offer, then apply for the scholarship through the AUS scholarship portal by 1 April 2027, so leave time for the admission process.

Application-fee waiver
For applicants schooled outside the UAE

aus-chancellors-scholarship-2027.about:
The Chancellor's Scholarship is the American University of Sharjah's most comprehensive award, open to applicants who completed their secondary education in the UAE, including expatriate students of any nationality. It covers full tuition and lab fees, an application-fee waiver, on-campus housing and student medical insurance.

Applicants need a 98% cumulative average in grades 10 and 11 plus 98% in grade 12 (or the equivalent: for example, the National Curriculum Elite Stream, or ATAR 96+ for Australian qualifications), AUS's English requirement, and two AP exams at grade 5 or an SAT composite of 1200+. The scholarship file also asks for evidence of leadership and contributions (honours, community service, extracurriculars), a three-minute video explaining why you should be selected and two letters of recommendation.

You must first be admitted to AUS, then submit the scholarship application through the AUS portal by 1 April 2027.
highlights: Full tuition and lab fees plus on-campus housing
Medical insurance and application-fee waiver
Open to any nationality schooled in the UAE
aus-chancellors-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Students of any nationality who completed secondary school in the UAE, hold an AUS offer for Fall 2027, have 98% averages (or equivalent), meet English requirements and have two AP 5s or SAT 1200+.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to AUS for Fall 2027
Submit predicted AP grades or SAT scores with the admission application
After admission, submit the Chancellor's Scholarship application with a 3-minute video and two recommendation letters by 1 Apr 2027
aus-chancellors-scholarship-2027.costs: Full tuition and lab fees, application-fee waiver, on-campus housing and student medical insurance.

uaeu-chancellors-scholarship-elite-stude.about:
The United Arab Emirates University in Al Ain is the country's first and largest federal university. Since 2025/2026 it has offered tuition discounts to international students under the Chancellor's Scholarship for Elite Students. The top level gives a 100% tuition waiver to applicants with at least 98% in grade 12 (or equivalent), TOEFL iBT 105 / IELTS 7.5, and (for most colleges) SAT Math 730 or ACT Math 32. A second level gives a 75% waiver for 95%+, TOEFL 85 / IELTS 6.5 and SAT Math 660 / ACT Math 28. There is also a Chancellor's Scholarship for Talented Students (innovation, arts, sport, technology).

The waiver covers tuition only (not housing or application fees) and continues until graduation if you keep a GPA of at least 3.8 (100% level) or 3.6 (75% level), take 15+ credits per semester and hold no other scholarship. Meeting the criteria does not guarantee an award; seats are limited.

There is no separate form: you apply for the scholarship as part of the UAEU admission application during the announced undergraduate admission periods for international students.
highlights: 100% tuition waiver for 98%+ (75% for 95%+)
Renewable to graduation with a high GPA
Requested inside the admission application
uaeu-chancellors-scholarship-elite-stude.eligibility: International students (from inside or outside the UAE) admitted to a UAEU bachelor's programme with the required grade-12 average, English scores (TOEFL iBT 105 / IELTS 7.5 for 100%) and maths scores (SAT Math 730 / ACT Math 32 for most colleges). Some programmes (e.g. MD) have extra restrictions.
how_to_apply: Watch the UAEU admissions site for the Fall 2027 international admission period
Prepare TOEFL/IELTS and SAT/ACT Math scores
Apply for admission online and request the Chancellor's Scholarship in the same application
Keep the required GPA and credit load to renew
uaeu-chancellors-scholarship-elite-stude.costs: Tuition waiver of 100% or 75%; housing and application fees are not covered.

hbku-undergraduate-financial-aid-2027.about:
Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU), a research university founded by Qatar Foundation, is best known for graduate study but has opened undergraduate admissions, currently for Honours Bachelor of Science degrees in Mechanical Engineering and Electrical Engineering at its College of Science and Engineering in Education City, Doha.

HBKU states that need-based financial aid is available for admitted undergraduate students, applied for after admission decisions. The amount depends on your family's financial situation; HBKU does not publish a fixed percentage, so treat it as partial-to-substantial support rather than a guaranteed full ride. Qatari students may also be eligible for national scholarships.

Apply online between 1 September 2026 and 1 March 2027 (up to two programmes per year), upload your documents and referee details, and sit IELTS or TOEFL (mandatory; SAT/ACT optional).
highlights: Honours BSc in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering
Need-based aid for admitted students
Test-optional for SAT/ACT; IELTS/TOEFL required
hbku-undergraduate-financial-aid-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school graduates of any nationality meeting HBKU's undergraduate requirements, with IELTS or TOEFL scores. Financial aid is need-based and applied for after admission.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the HBKU application portal (open from 1 Sep 2026)
Choose up to two programmes and submit the application by 1 Mar 2027
Upload documents and provide referee details as instructed by email
After the admission decision, apply for need-based financial aid
hbku-undergraduate-financial-aid-2027.costs: Need-based aid amount set individually after admission; tuition otherwise payable. Qatar Foundation and national scholarships may apply for some students.

kfupm-international-undergraduate-schola.about:
King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (KFUPM) in Dhahran is Saudi Arabia's leading science and engineering university, with all courses taught in English and close links to the energy and technology industries. For undergraduate international students living outside Saudi Arabia, tuition is waived and students receive a full scholarship whose benefits can include free on-campus housing, free course texts, a monthly stipend and medical services at the campus clinic.

The SAT Track is for graduates (current or previous year) of a high school with a natural sciences focus who score 1350 or above on the SAT. You send your scores to KFUPM through the College Board; once verified, KFUPM invites you to its own maths assessment, then to complete the online application, and it handles the visa after acceptance. A separate track guarantees admission and a full scholarship to the top four ISEF winners each year.

KFUPM does not publish a single closing date on its international page, so contact the Undergraduate Admissions team early in 2027 to confirm the window for the next intake.
highlights: Tuition waived plus free housing and monthly stipend
All programmes taught in English
Visa handled by KFUPM after admission
kfupm-international-undergraduate-schola.eligibility: International students living outside Saudi Arabia who graduated (this year or last) from a high school with a natural-sciences track and have an SAT score of 1350+; or top-four ISEF winners.
how_to_apply: Take the SAT and score 1350 or more
Send your SAT scores to 'King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals' via College Board
Take the KFUPM maths assessment when invited
Complete the online application on the KFUPM admissions website
After acceptance, KFUPM processes your visa
kfupm-international-undergraduate-schola.costs: Full scholarship: tuition waiver, free on-campus housing, monthly stipend, course texts and medical services.

gks-undergraduate-university-track-uic-2.about:
The Global Korea Scholarship for Undergraduate Degrees (GKS-U), run by Korea's National Institute for International Education (NIIED), is one of Asia's most complete government scholarships. Scholars first take a one-year Korean language programme, then a 4–6 year bachelor's degree at a Korean university. NIIED pays up to KRW 5 million of tuition per semester (the university waives the rest and the admission fee), the language programme fee, an economy return flight, and a monthly allowance of KRW 1,200,000 during the degree (KRW 1,130,000 during language study) covering living costs, housing and health insurance.

For 2027 the Embassy Track closed on 30 September 2026, but the University Track still runs through November 2026. Its UIC (University-Industry Cooperation) programme offers 100 places at 13 institutions, is open to applicants from every country, and combines the degree with industry-oriented curriculum and field experience. Embassy-track applicants who failed round one can also apply here.

Important eligibility point: you must be under 25 (born on or after 1 March 2002) and have graduated from high school, or be expected to graduate, by 31 December 2026, with an 80%+ average or a top-20% class rank. Students finishing school in mid-2027 must wait for the GKS-U 2028 call (expected September 2027).
highlights: Tuition + Korean language year + flights + KRW 1.2m/month
UIC programme open to all countries (100 places)
Final results expected by 7 Jan 2027
gks-undergraduate-university-track-uic-2.eligibility: Non-Korean citizens (and parents non-Korean) under 25 (born on or after 1 Mar 2002), who graduated from high school or will graduate by 31 Dec 2026, with a CGPA of 80%+ or top 20% of class, in good health and without a bachelor's degree.
how_to_apply: Download the 2027 GKS-U guidelines and UIC university list from Study in Korea
Check the chosen UIC university's own November 2026 deadline and submission method
Apply to one University Track programme with the required forms, transcripts and recommendation
If selected by the university, your documents go to NIIED by 30 Nov 2026; results by mid-December, final list ~7 Jan 2027
gks-undergraduate-university-track-uic-2.costs: NIIED: tuition up to KRW 5m/semester (university covers the rest), Korean language fee, economy airfare, KRW 1,200,000/month during the degree (KRW 1,130,000 during language study). Domestic travel and travel insurance are not covered.

nagoya-university-g30-undergraduate-scho.about:
Nagoya University is one of Japan's leading national research universities. Through its Global 30 (G30) International Programs it offers fully English-taught bachelor's degrees, starting in October, including Automotive Engineering, Civil and Environmental Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Biological Science, Earth and Environmental Sciences, Biological and Bioagricultural Sciences, Economics and Business Administration, Law and Political Science, and Japan-in-Asia Cultural Studies.

According to the G30 site, roughly 10–15% of students receive a full scholarship covering tuition and offering a small to moderate stipend, awarded after a holistic review of academic merit, extracurricular engagement and financial need. Admitted students in need can also get registration and tuition fee waivers of 50–100%, and self-financed students may receive the government's Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship (JPY 48,000/month for six months). The Japanese Government (MEXT) Embassy Recommendation scholarship (JPY 117,000/month) is a separate route with embassy applications in spring.

The 2027 first-round application window is 2–19 November 2026; a second round for a limited set of programmes runs 5–21 January 2027.
highlights: Full scholarships (tuition + stipend) for ~10–15% of students
50–100% tuition waivers for students in need
English-taught degrees at a top Japanese national university
nagoya-university-g30-undergraduate-scho.eligibility: International applicants who completed (or will complete) 12 years of schooling and meet G30 programme requirements (English proficiency, subject tests such as SAT/AP/IB/A-level depending on the programme). Scholarships are awarded holistically on merit and need.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 G30 undergraduate admission requirements
Register on the G30 online application portal
Submit your application and documents between 2 and 19 Nov 2026 (or 5–21 Jan 2027 for 2nd-round programmes)
Indicate financial need/scholarship interest as instructed; scholarship decisions follow admission
nagoya-university-g30-undergraduate-scho.costs: Full scholarship (tuition + stipend) for a minority; others may get 50–100% tuition waivers or short-term government honours stipends.

anu-chancellors-international-scholarshi.about:
The Australian National University in Canberra is consistently Australia's highest-ranked university. Its Chancellor's International Scholarship rewards academic merit among commencing international students: the undergraduate award is a 25% reduction of tuition fees, while citizens of South-East Asia, and of Europe, Central and South America, can receive 25% or 50%. Applicants are always assessed first for the highest-value award they qualify for, and the reduction continues for the standard length of the degree with a full-time load.

There is nothing extra to submit: every eligible overseas student who applies for admission to an eligible ANU programme (all except a few such as Medicine) is automatically considered, all year round. Up to 200 scholarships are on offer. You cannot hold another sponsorship that already covers your ANU tuition.
highlights: 25% (or 50% for some regions) off tuition for the whole degree
Automatic: no application
Up to 200 awards, assessed all year
anu-chancellors-international-scholarshi.eligibility: Commencing international (overseas) students with an offer to an eligible ANU bachelor's programme, ranked on the qualification used for admission; not holding external tuition sponsorship.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an ANU undergraduate programme
You are automatically assessed for the scholarship based on your results
The award is stated in or alongside your offer
anu-chancellors-international-scholarshi.costs: 25% tuition reduction (25% or 50% for South-East Asia, Europe and Central/South America) for the degree; living costs not covered.

hkust-admission-scholarships-internation.about:
HKUST is one of Asia's leading universities for science, engineering and business (6th in the QS Asia University Rankings 2026 and 33rd in the QS World University Rankings 2027, as HKUST reports). All applicants are automatically considered for academic admission scholarships, with no separate application. For holders of international qualifications such as IB, A-levels, AP/SAT or national diplomas, awards may be one-off or renewable and may fully or partially waive tuition; the largest is full tuition plus an allowance of HK$65,000 per year, renewable for the normal length of study.

The Global Learners Scholarship, created to diversify the student body, automatically considers all applicants from under-represented nationalities and gives successful awardees a full tuition waiver for the normal duration of study. Separate applications are needed for non-academic awards such as the Beyond Academic Admissions Scholarship and the new Future Leaders Award.

Applications for 2027/28 are open now. Apply by the Priority Round deadline of 25 November 2026 for the best chance; applications are accepted on a rolling basis afterwards until 30 June 2027. Scholarship decisions normally arrive with the admission offer.
highlights: Up to full tuition + HK$65,000 a year, renewable
Full tuition waiver for under-represented nationalities
Automatic consideration; priority deadline 25 Nov 2026
hkust-admission-scholarships-internation.eligibility: Applicants to HKUST undergraduate programmes with international or other non-local qualifications, of any nationality. Selection is holistic on academic merit; Global Learners targets nationalities under-represented at HKUST.
how_to_apply: Apply online for 2027/28 entry with your international qualification
Submit before the Priority Round deadline of 25 Nov 2026 (rolling to 30 Jun 2027)
Apply separately for non-academic awards (BAAS, Future Leaders Award) if relevant
Scholarship decisions come with your admission offer
hkust-admission-scholarships-internation.costs: Ranges from partial tuition waivers to full tuition plus HK$65,000 per year; Global Learners: full tuition waiver.

duke-kunshan-international-aid-2027.about:
Duke Kunshan University (DKU), near Shanghai, is a joint venture of Duke University, Wuhan University and the city of Kunshan. Undergraduates earn both a Duke University degree and a DKU degree through an interdisciplinary liberal arts curriculum taught in English, with opportunities to study at Duke in North Carolina.

International applicants can receive both need-based financial aid and merit scholarships that typically cover up to, and including, full tuition; more than 80% of international students received financial aid and/or scholarships last year, and awards are renewed annually for four years if requirements are met. For the Class of 2031, full cost-of-attendance Global Leaders Full Scholarship Awards are available for a very select few international students (extra application required). DKU is need-aware, so request aid only if you need it, but note that students who do not apply for aid at the admission stage cannot apply later.

Apply via the Common App (no application fee) by 2 November 2026 (Early Decision) or 4 January 2027 (Regular Decision), and submit the CSS Profile (DKU code 7059) if seeking need-based aid.
highlights: Duke University degree earned in China
Aid and merit typically up to full tuition; 80%+ of internationals funded
No application fee
duke-kunshan-international-aid-2027.eligibility: International (non-Chinese-citizen) first-year applicants via the Common App. Need-based aid requires the CSS Profile; Global Leaders Full Scholarship requires an additional application by the admission deadline.
how_to_apply: Submit the Common App to Duke Kunshan by 4 Jan 2027 (or ED 2 Nov 2026)
Answer 'yes' to financial aid and submit the CSS Profile (code 7059) if you need aid
If eligible, submit the separate Global Leaders Full Scholarship application
Receive scholarship/aid decisions with your admission offer
duke-kunshan-international-aid-2027.costs: Merit and/or need-based awards usually up to full tuition (renewable); a few full cost-of-attendance Global Leaders awards.

bocconi4access-tuition-waivers-2027.about:
Bocconi University in Milan, one of Europe's leading schools for economics, finance, management, law and data science, funds first-year bachelor's students through one application called Bocconi4Access to Education. For 2027-28 first-year tuition is €17,700, and the scheme can reduce it by 20% to 100%: full (100%) waivers and 80%/60% partial waivers under Bocconi4Access, and 40%/20% waivers under the Boost your Future scholarship for students who still need significant help.

Awards are based on the economic and asset situation of your family household, assessed by Bocconi's Fees, Funding and Housing Office, and are allocated until the budget runs out, so applying in an early session matters. Waivers renew for the legal duration of the course if you meet merit requirements. Separate non-means-tested waivers exist (Women award, siblings, sport, disability), and from year two the best students can win full-tuition Excellence awards.
highlights: Tuition waivers of 100%, 80%, 60%, 40% or 20% on €17,700/year
One application covers all need-based levels
Renewable for the whole degree with good grades
bocconi4access-tuition-waivers-2027.eligibility: International applicants (non-Italian school system) admitted to the first year of a Bocconi Bachelor of Science or Law programme in 2027-28, with documented family income and assets. Applicants must be at least 17 on 1 September 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply to a Bocconi bachelor's programme in one of the 2027-28 admission sessions (online test + application)
Submit the single 'Bocconi4Access to Education a.y. 2027-28' funding application with family financial documents
Meet the funding deadline for your session (check the timeline page)
Receive the funding outcome and enrol within about three weeks of admission results
bocconi4access-tuition-waivers-2027.costs: Tuition €17,700 per year (2027-28 first year), reduced by 20–100%. Living costs in Milan (about €1,000–1,400/month) are not covered by the waiver.

padua-international-excellence-scholarsh.about:
The University of Padua, founded in 1222 and one of Italy's top research universities, awards up to 76 Padua International Excellence Scholarships across its English-taught bachelor's and master's degrees. Each scholarship pays €8,000 gross per academic year (two instalments of €4,000) and waives university tuition, so winners pay only the regional tax and a revenue stamp. Bachelor's and single-cycle students can hold it for up to three years.

There is no separate form: applying to an eligible English-taught degree before the admission deadline automatically enters you, and each degree's Teaching Committee selects winners on academic excellence and prior record, mainly in the first call. To keep the award you must earn at least 20 ECTS credits by 30 November of the following year. Padua also offers 100 separate full fee waivers for international students in English-taught degrees.
highlights: €8,000 per year + tuition waiver for up to 3 years
Automatic consideration when you apply to an English-taught degree
Up to 76 awards across bachelor's and master's
padua-international-excellence-scholarsh.eligibility: Non-Italian citizens (dual citizens allowed) with a non-Italian secondary-school diploma, not resident in Italy, applying to a Padua degree taught entirely in English, not holding other scholarships.
how_to_apply: Choose an English-taught bachelor's programme at Padua
Apply for admission in the first call (calls published November 2026)
Upload CV, transcripts, motivation and language certificates — these are used for the scholarship ranking
If selected, accept the offer and enrol by the deadline
padua-international-excellence-scholarsh.costs: €8,000 gross per year plus waiver of university tuition; winners pay only the regional tax (about €170) and a €16 stamp. Accommodation in Padua costs roughly €350–550/month.

padua-full-fee-waivers-international-202.about:
Alongside its excellence scholarships, the University of Padua grants 100 full waivers of university tuition fees to international students who enrol in degree programmes taught entirely in English. Bachelor's and single-cycle students can renew the waiver into the third year.

There is no separate application: candidates are ranked on their admission file (CV, personal statement, transcripts, language skills), and winners must accept the admission offer, pay the first instalment and meet enrolment conditions. The waiver removes tuition but not living costs, so it pairs well with the Veneto regional (ESU) need-based grant.
highlights: 100 full tuition waivers per year
Automatic — based on your admission application
Open to all nationalities with a foreign school diploma
padua-full-fee-waivers-international-202.eligibility: Non-Italian citizens (unless dual), with a foreign secondary-school diploma, not resident in Italy, applying within the deadlines to an English-taught Padua degree.
how_to_apply: Apply to an English-taught bachelor's at Padua in the 2027/28 admission call
Submit a strong CV, personal statement and language certificates
Check the results list; accept the offer and enrol by the deadline
padua-full-fee-waivers-international-202.costs: Waiver of university tuition (international fees otherwise up to about €2,700/year, income-based). Regional tax, stamp and living costs remain.

laziodisco-regional-scholarship-2027.about:
In Italy, regional 'right to study' (DSU) agencies give means-tested scholarships to students at public universities, and international students are eligible on the same basis as Italians. DiSCo Lazio serves universities in Rome and the Lazio region, including Sapienza, Tor Vergata and Roma Tre. Winners typically receive a cash scholarship (larger for students living away from home), exemption from university tuition, and access to subsidised housing and canteens.

Eligibility depends on family income and assets, calculated for foreign families through an 'ISEE parificato' using documents from your home country (income, property, family composition), translated and legalised. First-year awards are confirmed once you earn the required credits. The call is strict and non-extendable, so start collecting documents as soon as you apply to your university.
highlights: Cash grant + tuition exemption + possible housing and meals
Open to international students at Rome's public universities
Strict summer deadline — prepare home-country income documents early
laziodisco-regional-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Students (any nationality) enrolling at a public university or institution in Lazio whose family income/assets fall below the call's ISEE/ISPE thresholds; first-year students must later meet credit requirements.
how_to_apply: Apply and get admitted to a public university in Rome/Lazio
Collect family income, property and household documents from your home country; translate and legalise them
Obtain the Italian tax code and the ISEE parificato through an authorised CAF
Submit the online application in the DiSCo reserved area before the call deadline (est. July 2027)
laziodisco-regional-scholarship-2027.costs: Means-tested cash grant (amount depends on income and on-site/commuter/off-site status), plus tuition exemption and possible housing/meal services. Exact 2027/28 amounts will be set in the call.

ergo-emilia-romagna-scholarship-2027.about:
ER.GO is the regional right-to-study agency for Emilia-Romagna, home to the University of Bologna (the world's oldest university) and the universities of Modena and Reggio Emilia, Parma and Ferrara. In 2025/26 it invested over €160 million in scholarships and services. Winners receive a cash scholarship whose amount depends on family income and on whether they are resident, commuter or off-site students, plus a full exemption from university tuition, a refund of the regional tax, and the option to convert part of the grant into meal vouchers; off-site students can also apply for ER.GO housing.

International students qualify under the same economic and merit rules, with family income certified from home-country documents. ER.GO runs a dedicated International Students section with step-by-step guides, including how to get an Italian tax code.
highlights: Cash grant + full tuition exemption + regional tax refund
Covers Bologna, Modena-Reggio, Parma and Ferrara universities
English-language guides for international applicants
ergo-emilia-romagna-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Students of any nationality enrolling at a university in Emilia-Romagna whose family economic indicators are below the ER.GO thresholds, meeting merit (credit) requirements from the second year.
how_to_apply: Apply to your degree at Bologna, Modena-Reggio Emilia, Parma or Ferrara
Get an Italian tax code and gather certified family income documents
Follow ER.GO's 'International students – how to apply' guide and submit online
Apply before the summer 2027 deadline (previous call: 24 August 2026)
ergo-emilia-romagna-scholarship-2027.costs: Cash scholarship scaled by income and residence status, full tuition exemption, regional-tax refund; housing for off-site students on request.

ie-university-undergraduate-awards-2027.about:
IE University (Madrid and Segovia) is a private, highly international university known for business, international relations, law, architecture, computer science and data. Its undergraduate IE Awards are open to every nationality and programme and cover between 10% and 60% of tuition. They are assessed on both merit and financial need, so families must submit a financial questionnaire. Named awards include the IE Academic Achievement Award (for averages around 9/10, 3.8/4 GPA, IB 38/45 or equivalent), Personal Excellence (extracurriculars), Young Entrepreneurs, Women in STEM, Sustainability, Humanities and Collaboration awards. IE Foundation partner scholarships are listed separately and may require an extra essay.

Check coverage carefully: IE's standard awards are partial (up to 60% of tuition, which is about €20,000+ per year). Higher coverage comes only through specific partner or foundation scholarships. You can select up to three awards but receive only one, and awards renew each year if you meet renewal criteria.
highlights: 10%–60% of tuition, all nationalities and programmes
Merit + financial need; select up to 3 awards, receive 1
Rolling: decision 1–3 weeks after a complete application
ie-university-undergraduate-awards-2027.eligibility: Admitted (or newly admitted) applicants to an IE University bachelor's programme for 2027-28, any nationality. Specific awards add criteria (e.g. strong grades for Academic Achievement, women for Women in STEM, entrepreneurial track record for Young Entrepreneurs).
how_to_apply: Apply for admission in a 2027-28 round (deadlines 6 Nov 2026, 15 Jan 2027, 5 Mar 2027)
After receiving your offer, log in to the IE Financial Aid platform with your admission credentials
Choose up to three awards and upload the required documents/essays
Your parents complete the financial questionnaire; resolution arrives in 1–3 weeks
Enrol to secure the award
ie-university-undergraduate-awards-2027.costs: Award covers 10%–60% of tuition (bachelor's tuition at IE is roughly €22,000–€28,000+ per year). Living costs in Madrid are not covered.

esade-talent-scholarships-bachelor-2027.about:
Esade, one of Europe's top business and law schools, runs a €5 million Scholarship Program; about 8.4% of its undergraduates hold a scholarship, with an average 84% of tuition covered. Degree Talent Scholarships (Dedicated, Future and Class Talent Scholarships, named after their donors) cover between 60% and 100% of tuition for the entire BBA, Law, BITLASI or double-degree programme, based on academic results and financial need. Complements include Esade Lodging Grants for students who live outside Barcelona province and Esade Living Grants for transport and general expenses.

To qualify you need an average of 8.5/10 in the last two years of school or an equivalent: IB 33/42, French Bac 16.2/20, or 85% of the maximum in other systems, and SAT 1300+ if you submit the SAT. Family income must not exceed €118,000 gross a year for a family of four, with assets also assessed.
highlights: 60%–100% of tuition for the whole degree
Lodging and Living grants for students from outside Barcelona
Clear thresholds: IB 33+, 85% of max grade, family income ≤ €118,000 (family of 4)
esade-talent-scholarships-bachelor-2027.eligibility: Applicants admitted to an Esade bachelor's or double degree with an outstanding record (8.5/10, IB 33/42, French Bac 16.2/20, 85% of max elsewhere; SAT 1300+ if used) and family gross income up to €118,000/year for four people.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to your chosen Esade bachelor's (online; open until June 2027)
Sit the Esade Admission Test or submit other accepted tests
Once admitted, apply for the scholarship for your preferred programme via the scholarship application link
Submit family financial documentation; the scholarship then holds for your whole degree
esade-talent-scholarships-bachelor-2027.costs: 60%–100% of tuition (Esade bachelor's tuition is about €20,000+ per year). Lodging/Living grants can add support for accommodation and expenses.

esade-academic-merit-awards-bachelor-202.about:
Separate from its need-based Talent Scholarships, Esade offers Academic Merit Awards for bachelor's applicants with excellent records. They are renewable and can cover up to 100% of tuition. The programme includes the Best University Access Grade Award and the Academic Excellence and Distinction Awards, each with its own requirements.

You must already be admitted to your degree or double degree, then apply in the Candidate Portal following the award guide. The committee looks at your academic record at admission plus award-specific documents. You may apply for only one award; once granted it is not reviewed again, and it can be combined with a Talent Scholarship or Esade's Income-Share Agreement as long as the total does not exceed 100% of tuition.
highlights: Up to 100% of tuition, renewable
Purely merit-based (no income test)
Combinable with Talent Scholarships or ISA up to 100%
esade-academic-merit-awards-bachelor-202.eligibility: Students admitted to an Esade bachelor's or double degree for 2027-28 who meet the academic requirements of the specific award.
how_to_apply: Get admitted to an Esade bachelor's programme
Read the award orientation guide in your Candidate Portal
Submit the award application with the requested documents
Await the committee decision (communicated individually)
esade-academic-merit-awards-bachelor-202.costs: Covers a share of tuition up to 100%, depending on the award. Living costs not included.

university-of-navarra-alumni-scholarship.about:
The University of Navarra (Pamplona, with campuses in Madrid, San Sebastián and Barcelona) is a leading private Spanish university, highly ranked for medicine, communication, law, business and architecture. Its main undergraduate scholarship, the Beca Alumni, supports students with an excellent secondary-school record who face financial difficulties. The amount is personalised: the committee looks at tuition, housing costs, other scholarships and how much the family can contribute.

A newer University of Navarra Aid Programme gives personalised aid to students with good grades and demonstrated need. International students with top-5% class rank can also get a 16% first-year honours discount, and faculties offer their own awards (e.g. Prof. Jiménez Vargas Scholarship in Medicine). For 2027/28, admissions opened on 1 October 2026, with main rounds on 9 December 2026 and 9 March 2027.
highlights: Personalised amount covering tuition and possibly housing
For excellent students with financial need
Admission rounds 9 Dec 2026 and 9 Mar 2027
university-of-navarra-alumni-scholarship.eligibility: Applicants admitted to a University of Navarra degree (grado) with an excellent secondary-school record and demonstrated family financial difficulty. International students are eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to a degree for 2027/28 (rounds close 9 December 2026 and 9 March 2027)
Sit the university admission test on the scheduled date
Submit the Beca Alumni application with family financial documents (see regulations)
Receive the scholarship decision with or after your admission
university-of-navarra-alumni-scholarship.costs: Personalised amount towards tuition (about €11,000–€19,000+ per year depending on degree) and possibly housing.

koc-university-international-merit-schol.about:
Koç University in Istanbul is Türkiye's top-ranked private research university, teaching in English across business, economics, engineering, law, social sciences and natural sciences. Every admitted international undergraduate is evaluated by the Admissions Committee for a merit scholarship on academic merit only (need-blind), covering 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of annual tuition for the duration of the programme.

There is no separate scholarship application: results arrive with your admission offer. Strong standardised scores (SAT/ACT, IB, A-levels or equivalents) are essential, as applying without one significantly lowers both admission and scholarship chances. Merit scholarships cover tuition only (no housing or living costs), and the School of Medicine offers no scholarships to internationals. Country-specific programmes (e.g. Azerbaijan State Scholarship, HEC Pakistan, Türkiye Burslari at Koç) are listed separately.
highlights: 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of tuition for the full degree
Automatic and need-blind — results come with your offer
Apply early with SAT/ACT/IB/A-level scores
koc-university-international-merit-schol.eligibility: International applicants admitted to a Koç University undergraduate programme (except Medicine), with strong academic records and standardised test scores.
how_to_apply: Prepare SAT/ACT, IB or A-level results and English proficiency (e.g. TOEFL)
Apply online via Koç's international application portal in the early round (expected Jan–Mar 2027)
Upload transcripts, motivation letter and test scores
Receive your admission and scholarship decision together by email
koc-university-international-merit-schol.costs: Covers 25–100% of tuition (Koç international tuition is roughly US$30,000+ per year). Housing and living costs are not covered.

aalto-university-excellence-scholarship-.about:
Aalto University in Espoo (Helsinki region) is Finland's leading university for technology, business, and art and design. Non-EU/EEA students in its English-taught bachelor's programmes pay €12,000 a year (technology, business, multidisciplinary) or €15,000 (art and architecture). The Aalto University Excellence Scholarship waives the full tuition fee for the normative three years, provided you study full-time and on plan.

The award is merit-based and highly competitive, and programmes may choose not to award any. The application is part of the admission form, so you must request it during the 7–22 January 2027 joint application; waiting-list admits cannot receive it. Students without the scholarship who accept and pay within 21 days get 25% off first-year tuition. Living costs (at least €800/month) are not covered.
highlights: 100% tuition waiver for 3 years (worth €36,000–€45,000)
Apply inside the admission form, 7–22 January 2027
25% early-acceptance discount for non-scholarship admits
aalto-university-excellence-scholarship-.eligibility: Non-EU/EEA (and non-Swiss) citizens liable for tuition who apply to an Aalto English-taught bachelor's programme in the 2027 joint application (SAT/ACT-based round A or certificate-based round B).
how_to_apply: Choose an English-taught bachelor's programme (science & technology or business)
Apply on Opintopolku/Studyinfo between 7 and 22 January 2027 (round A for most international diplomas, with SAT/ACT)
Tick and complete the scholarship section in the same form
Submit required documents by the stated deadline; admission and scholarship results come together
aalto-university-excellence-scholarship-.costs: Waives €12,000–€15,000 tuition per year. Living costs of at least €800/month (and the residence-permit funds requirement) must be self-funded.

tampere-university-tuition-fee-scholarsh.about:
Tampere University, Finland's second-largest multidisciplinary university, charges €10,000 a year for its English-taught bachelor's programmes to students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. Its tuition fee scholarship covers 50% of tuition for the programme duration for merited, high-achieving and motivated fee-paying students.

Awards are very limited (only nine across all bachelor's and master's programmes in 2026) and not every programme offers them. You apply in the same Studyinfo.fi admission application, and the committee judges your educational documents and any scholarship letter, sending the decision with your admission result. Fee-paying students who don't win can get a €2,000 first-year early-bird reduction by accepting and paying within 21 days.
highlights: 50% of €10,000 annual tuition for the whole programme
Apply inside the Studyinfo.fi admission form
€2,000 early-bird discount as a fallback
tampere-university-tuition-fee-scholarsh.eligibility: Citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland applying to an English-taught Tampere bachelor's programme that offers scholarships, with an excellent academic record.
how_to_apply: Pick an English-taught bachelor's programme at Tampere
Apply on Studyinfo.fi during the January 2027 joint application
Complete the scholarship part (and letter, if requested) in the same form
Receive the scholarship decision with your admission result
tampere-university-tuition-fee-scholarsh.costs: Scholarship halves the €10,000 annual tuition. Living costs (around €800–1,000/month) are not covered.

radboud-scholarship-programme-2027.about:
The Radboud Scholarship Programme is Radboud University's merit scholarship for excellent students from outside the EU/EEA who are admitted to an English-taught master's programme in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, starting 1 September 2027.

Instead of the full non-EU fee (up to about €19,000 a year depending on the programme), scholarship holders pay roughly the Dutch statutory fee (about €2,771, to be confirmed). The scholarship also pays for the visa and residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance. It does not cover living costs, but it can be combined with the NL Scholarship.

You apply by ticking the scholarship option in your master's application in OSIRIS and uploading two reference letters and a CV. Submit by 31 January 2027 and make sure the application is complete by 14 February 2027; decisions come in mid-April. Selection is separate from admission.
highlights: Tuition reduced to about the Dutch statutory fee (~€2,771)
Visa, residence permit and insurance covered
Deadline 31 January 2027
radboud-scholarship-programme-2027.eligibility: Non-EU/EEA passport holders who do not qualify for the EU tuition rate; bachelor's degree from outside the Netherlands with no previous Dutch education; English requirement met; full admission to an English-taught master's starting 1 September 2027; able to meet Dutch visa conditions. Erasmus Mundus and joint-degree master's are excluded. Open to Georgian and Qatari citizens.
how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible English-taught master's in OSIRIS
Select the Radboud Scholarship Programme option in the application
Upload a CV and two reference letters
Submit by 31 January 2027 and complete everything by 14 February 2027
radboud-scholarship-programme-2027.costs: You pay about €2,771 tuition instead of up to ~€19,000 (2027/28 example). Visa, residence permit, health and liability insurance are covered. Living costs (about €1,000–1,300 a month in the Netherlands) are not covered.

university-of-twente-scholarship-2027.about:
The University of Twente Scholarship (UTS) supports excellent non-EU/EEA students in master's programmes at the University of Twente in Enschede, a leading Dutch technical university known for engineering, computer science, business and the ITC faculty.

Awards range from €3,000 to €22,000 for the first year, as a contribution to study costs (not a full scholarship). For two-year master's, the same amount can be paid in year two if you reach an average grade of 7/10 and at least 50% of credits by the end of the third quartile. UTS holders can also indicate interest in the Kipaji Scholarship.

You must be in the top 5–10% of your graduating class and have IELTS 6.5 (speaking 6.0) or TOEFL iBT 90. Apply for your master's first, wait for (conditional) admission, then submit the UTS form with your student number between 15 October 2026 and 1 April 2027.
highlights: €3,000–22,000 for year 1, renewable for year 2
For top 5–10% non-EU graduates
Deadline 1 April 2027
university-of-twente-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Non-EU/EEA citizens (provisionally) admitted to a qualifying UT master's starting September 2027; top 5–10% of their class; IELTS 6.5 (speaking 6.0) or TOEFL iBT 90 (speaking 20); not eligible for Dutch loans or EU-level fees; not current UT students or graduates. ITC master's and pre-master students are excluded.
how_to_apply: Apply for a UT master's programme
Wait for your (conditional) admission letter and student number (up to 8 weeks)
Fill in the UTS application form with your student number and motivation
Submit before 1 April 2027, 16:00 CET
university-of-twente-scholarship-2027.costs: €3,000 to €22,000 for the first year (and possibly the same for year two). Non-EU tuition and Dutch living costs are much higher, so you need additional funds.

eric-bleumink-fund-2027.about:
The Eric Bleumink Fund, named after a former rector, gives a small number of full fellowships each year to excellent students from developing countries for one- or two-year master's programmes at the University of Groningen starting in September.

The fellowship covers tuition, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance. Recipients are expected to return home and contribute to their country's development.

There is no direct application: the Admission Office and faculty admission boards nominate candidates from among master's applicants. To be considered, submit your complete master's application before 1 December 2026 and secure provisional or unconditional admission before February 2027.
highlights: Full package: tuition, travel, living costs, books, insurance
No separate form: nomination from your master's application
Apply to your master's by 1 December 2026
eric-bleumink-fund-2027.eligibility: Citizens of the developing countries listed in Appendix 1 of the official page (e.g. Bangladesh, Ghana, India, Kenya, Nigeria, Pakistan, Vietnam); excellent academic record; admission to a one- or two-year Groningen master's starting in September. Check the appendix for Georgia; Qatar is not a developing-country listing.
how_to_apply: Choose a University of Groningen master's starting September 2027
Submit a complete application before 1 December 2026
Obtain provisional or unconditional admission before February 2027
If nominated by the admission board, the university contacts you
eric-bleumink-fund-2027.costs: Covers tuition fees, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance.

padua-international-excellence-2027.about:
The University of Padua, one of Europe's oldest universities (founded 1222), offers International Excellence Scholarships to the best international applicants to its English-taught master's degrees in fields such as data science, engineering, economics, psychology and life sciences.

Each scholarship is worth €8,000 gross per year (paid in two instalments) for up to two years, plus exemption from tuition; holders pay only the regional tax and a revenue stamp. Keeping the award depends on earning enough credits (at least 20 ECTS by 30 November of the following year).

There is no separate scholarship form: applying to the master's in the first call makes you eligible, and each teaching committee ranks candidates on academic merit. The 2027/28 calls are due to be published in November 2026, with deadlines in each programme's admission notice.
highlights: €8,000/year + tuition waiver for up to 2 years
No separate application: apply to an English-taught master's
2027/28 calls published November 2026
padua-international-excellence-2027.eligibility: Non-Italian citizens (dual nationals excepted) with a foreign degree, not resident in Italy at application, applying to an English-taught Padua master's in the first call. Cannot be combined with other scholarships. Open to Georgian and Qatari citizens.
how_to_apply: Choose an English-taught master's at the University of Padua
Read the 2027/28 admission notice once published (November 2026)
Apply in the first admission call with transcripts, CV and documents
The teaching committee ranks applicants and awards scholarships
padua-international-excellence-2027.costs: €8,000 gross per academic year plus tuition exemption (only the regional fee and a revenue stamp are paid). After the funded period, tuition applies until graduation.

adb-japan-scholarship-program-2027.about:
The ADB–Japan Scholarship Program, funded by Japan and run by the Asian Development Bank since 1988, offers about 130 scholarships a year for master's study at 27 designated institutions in Asia and the Pacific, 17 of them in Japan (for example GRIPS, Hitotsubashi, Keio, the University of Tokyo and others listed on adb.org).

It is for early-career professionals from ADB developing member countries: you need a strong bachelor's record, at least two years of full-time work, be 35 or younger, live and work in your home country, and agree to work there for two years after graduating.

You apply to a participating master's programme and submit the JSP information sheet with your application; the institution shortlists and ADB makes the final selection. Benefits include full tuition, a monthly allowance with housing, books, medical insurance and travel.
highlights: Full tuition, monthly allowance (incl. housing), insurance and travel
27 partner institutions, 17 in Japan
For professionals aged 35 or under with 2+ years' experience
adb-japan-scholarship-program-2027.eligibility: Citizens of ADB borrowing developing member countries that are also eligible for Japanese ODA scholarships (e.g. Afghanistan, Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, the Philippines, Viet Nam, Pacific island states; Georgia is an ADB member, so check the list). Bachelor's with a superior record, two years' full-time work experience, aged 35 or under, admitted to an approved master's, good English, living in the home country, not a dual citizen of a developed country.
how_to_apply: Choose a designated institution and programme from ADB's list
Request admission and JSP application forms from that institution
Submit the admission application with the JSP information sheet by the institution's deadline
The institution shortlists; ADB makes the final selection
adb-japan-scholarship-program-2027.costs: Full tuition; monthly subsistence and housing allowance; books and instructional materials; medical insurance; travel expenses; possible thesis grant for research scholars.

kfupm-graduate-scholarship-2027.about:
