King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals in Dhahran is Saudi Arabia's leading engineering and science university. It awards full scholarships to international graduate students in all PhD programmes and in selected thesis-based MS programmes that do not have a corresponding doctoral track.

Scholars get free tuition, a monthly stipend set by scholarship category, free furnished on-campus housing with utilities, round-trip air tickets and medical and dental care. MS applicants need a four-year engineering or science bachelor's with GPA 3.00/4.00 for scholarship consideration and English (TOEFL iBT 70, IELTS 6.0 or Duolingo 105); PhD applicants need a relevant master's with GPA 3.00 and TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 120. Direct-entry PhD from a bachelor's is possible.

The College of Graduate Studies lists an application window of 1 November to 15 December 2026 for thesis-based MS and PhD programmes, with applications through apply.kfupm.edu.sa and decisions in two to three months.
highlights: Free tuition, monthly stipend, campus housing, flights and medical care
All PhD programmes and selected thesis-based MS programmes
Application window 1 Nov–15 Dec 2026
kfupm-graduate-scholarship-2027.eligibility: International applicants of any nationality. MS: four-year bachelor's in engineering or science, GPA ≥ 3.00/4.00 for scholarship, TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6.0 / Duolingo 105, two recommendation letters. PhD: relevant master's with GPA ≥ 3.00 in BS and MS, TOEFL iBT 80 / IELTS 6.5 / Duolingo 120. English tests waived for graduates of KFUPM and of universities in the USA, Canada, UK, Australia and New Zealand.
how_to_apply: Choose a thesis-based MS or PhD programme at KFUPM
Take TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo and send scores (TOEFL code 0868)
Apply online at apply.kfupm.edu.sa between 1 November and 15 December 2026
Arrange two recommendation letters through the online system
Attend an interview if invited; decisions take 2–3 months
kfupm-graduate-scholarship-2027.costs: Tuition-free; monthly stipend based on scholarship category; free furnished on-campus housing with utilities; round-trip air tickets; medical and dental care.

fulbright-foreign-student-program-2028.about:
The Fulbright Foreign Student Program brings graduate students, young professionals and artists from more than 160 countries to study and research in the United States, with about 4,000 new grants each year. Most awards fund a one- or two-year master's degree; some countries also fund PhD study or non-degree research.

Everything is run nationally. The binational Fulbright commission or the US embassy in your country decides eligibility, fields, deadlines and interviews, and either IIE places you at US universities (IIE-placement) or you apply to universities yourself (self-placement). Grants typically cover tuition, a living stipend, health coverage and travel, though the package varies by country.

Deadlines for study starting in 2027 have mostly passed. For 2028–29, country calls generally open in early 2027 and close between February and October 2027, so now is the time to take the TOEFL/IELTS and GRE where needed and watch your national Fulbright page. Georgia has its own Fulbright Graduate Student Program run by the US Embassy in Tbilisi.
highlights: About 4,000 grants a year in 160+ countries
Usually covers tuition, stipend, insurance and travel
Apply through your country's Fulbright commission or US embassy
fulbright-foreign-student-program-2028.eligibility: Citizens of participating countries (rules set nationally), usually with a bachelor's degree, strong English (TOEFL/IELTS) and, for many countries, a commitment to return home after the grant (J-1 visa two-year home-residency rule). People who already hold a PhD are generally not eligible. Check your country's page for age and field rules.
how_to_apply: Find your country on the Fulbright Foreign Student website
Open your national Fulbright commission or US embassy page for 2028–29 rules
Prepare English and graduate test scores, transcripts, study objectives and references
Submit the national application (often via apply.iie.org) by your country's deadline
Attend the national interview if shortlisted
fulbright-foreign-student-program-2028.costs: Depends on the country, but grants generally cover tuition and fees (or IIE-negotiated waivers), a monthly living stipend, health benefits and round-trip travel.

sxsw-pitch-2027.about:
SXSW Pitch is a flagship event of the South by Southwest festival in Austin. Through an open call, startups from around the world apply in one of several categories, for example Emerging & Frontier Technologies (robotics, AI hardware, semiconductors, quantum, space), Entertainment, Media, Sports & Digital Platforms, Smart Data/Security/FinTech, and Healthcare/AssistiveTech/BioTech. Finalists pitch live on stage at SXSW in March 2027 to a panel of industry experts, early adopters and investors, and winners are announced at an awards ceremony.

Applications for 2027 opened on 23 June 2026; regular entry runs 14 September to 13 November 2026 with a $225 fee (non-refundable even if not selected). Finalists gain huge visibility in the SXSW press and investor community.

Best for student founders who already have a product with technical differentiation and can travel to Austin.
highlights: 19th edition, global open call
Live pitch at SXSW in Austin before investors and media
Multiple technology categories
sxsw-pitch-2027.eligibility: Startups from any country with a working product or strong technology; categories have specific requirements (e.g. defensible IP for frontier tech). Finalists must attend SXSW in Austin. English.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 categories and rules on sxsw.com/pitch
Prepare your company description, video and deck
Apply and pay the $225 regular entry fee by 13 November 2026
Finalists are notified and pitch at SXSW in March 2027
sxsw-pitch-2027.costs: Application fee $225 (non-refundable). Travel and stay in Austin at your own cost; finalists receive event access (see rules).

techstars-startup-weekend.about:
Startup Weekend is a 54-hour event run by local organisers with Techstars. On Friday evening participants pitch ideas in 60 seconds; the group votes and teams form around the best ones. Over the weekend teams validate the problem with real customers, build a prototype or landing page and prepare a business model, with coaching from local mentors. On Sunday they demo to a panel of judges, often investors and founders.

More than 7,000 events have been held in 150+ countries with 428,000+ participants. There are general events and themed editions (education, health, women, AI, youth). You don't need an idea or technical skills to join: developers, designers and business people are all needed.

It is one of the best ways for a student to experience building a startup, meet co-founders and connect with the local ecosystem. You can also organise an event in your own city.
highlights: 7,000+ events in 150+ countries
No idea or experience required
Meet co-founders and mentors in one weekend
techstars-startup-weekend.eligibility: Open to anyone; most events welcome students (some set a minimum age, often 16 or 18). Language depends on the local event.
how_to_apply: Go to the Startup Weekend page on techstars.com and click 'Find an Event'
Choose an event in your city or online and buy/register a ticket
Prepare a 60-second pitch if you have an idea (optional)
Attend all three days and demo on Sunday
techstars-startup-weekend.costs: Tickets are set by local organisers, usually low cost and often discounted for students; meals during the weekend are usually included.

web-summit-lisbon-2027-startups.about:
Web Summit Lisbon brings together tens of thousands of attendees, thousands of startups, investors and media each November (the 2026 edition is on 9–12 November 2026). Its startup programme selects early-stage companies to exhibit for a day, take part in the PITCH competition, join investor meetings and office hours, and use the event app to book meetings with investors who have included Neil Shen, Fred Wilson, Reid Hoffman and Vinod Khosla.

The 2026 startup programme is sold out, and applications are now open for 2027 (exact 2027 dates are announced by Web Summit; it is traditionally held in November). The process: apply with a business email, a specialist team assesses and selects startups, and accepted companies prepare with Web Summit's startup success resources before the event.

It suits student founders who already have a product and want maximum exposure; there are package fees, so ask about discounts for very early startups.
highlights: Exhibit and pitch at one of the world's largest tech conferences
Investor meetings and office hours
Applications open now for 2027
web-summit-lisbon-2027-startups.eligibility: Early-stage startups from any country (selection by Web Summit's team). Students can also attend Web Summit with student tickets.
how_to_apply: Go to websummit.com/startups and click 'Apply for 2027'
Enter your business email and startup details
Discuss packages with the specialist team if selected
Prepare your stand, pitch and investor meetings
web-summit-lisbon-2027-startups.costs: Startup packages are paid (price depends on the programme); travel and accommodation in Lisbon at your own cost.

world-scout-jamboree-poland-2027.about:
The World Scout Jamboree takes place every four years and is the biggest educational event for young people anywhere. The 26th edition, themed 'Bravely', will be hosted by Poland in Gdańsk from 30 July to 8 August 2027, the first in Europe since Sweden 2011, and will mark 120 years of Scouting on 1 August 2027.

For ten days patrols of Scouts from 170+ countries live together on a giant campsite, cook for each other, take part in adventure, water, cultural, global-development and sustainability programmes, and visit Gdańsk and the Pomorskie region. Adults aged 18+ can serve on the International Service Team (IST) that runs the camp.

You cannot register individually: participants go as part of their country's official contingent, organised by the national Scout association that is a member of WOSM. Contingents set their own age bands (within WOSM rules), fees, selection and deadlines, and many are recruiting now. A Solidarity Operation fund helps Scouts from lower-income countries attend.
highlights: 50,000 participants from 170+ countries
Ten days of camp, adventure and culture in Gdańsk
Solidarity fund for Scouts from lower-income countries
world-scout-jamboree-poland-2027.eligibility: Members of a national Scout organisation recognised by WOSM, within the youth-participant age band set for the Jamboree (check with your contingent); adults 18+ can apply as International Service Team members or contingent leaders.
how_to_apply: Join or contact your national Scout association
Ask about the Jamboree 2027 contingent: age band, fee and deadline
Register through your contingent (individual registration is not possible)
Adults: apply for the International Service Team via your contingent
world-scout-jamboree-poland-2027.costs: Participant fees are set per country (WOSM fee scale plus travel); the Solidarity Operation helps fund Scouts from lower-income countries.

european-forum-alpbach-scholarship-2027.about:
The European Forum Alpbach (EFA) is one of Europe's most important forums on politics, economics, science and culture, held each summer in the Tyrolean village of Alpbach. EFA27 runs from 23 August to 3 September 2027, with the Conference Days opening on 29 August. Scholarship holders are the only participants who stay for the entire forum: they attend scientific, competence-based and artistic seminars and studios, take part in the high-level conference with European leaders, and join a social and cultural programme.

About 350 scholarships are awarded each year to first-time participants from all countries and disciplines; artists and non-graduates are welcome. The scholarship covers the participation fee and accommodation; extra support for food and travel can be requested if needed (subject to funds). Alumni join the Forum Alpbach Network of 34 initiatives in 20 countries.

Applications for 2027 open in March 2027 on alpbach.org. Many students from Georgia, the Western Balkans and the wider world have attended through this programme.
highlights: ~350 scholarships covering participation fee and accommodation
Open to all countries and disciplines; non-graduates and artists welcome
Seminars plus a high-level European conference in the Alps
european-forum-alpbach-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Aged 18–30 at the time of the Forum (18–35 for citizens of the Global South); first-time scholarship holders; English at B2 or above (proof required); able to attend the full duration (departures only from 31 August in justified cases).
how_to_apply: Read the Scholarship Programme page on alpbach.org
Prepare your latest academic record and proof of English (B2+)
Apply online when applications open in March 2027
Request additional support for travel/food in the application if needed
european-forum-alpbach-scholarship-2027.costs: Scholarship covers the participation fee and accommodation. Food and travel are your own unless additional support is granted. Applicants who can afford it are asked to pay their own accommodation (EFA26: €49/night).

exeter-summer-upper-school-2027.about:
Exeter Summer is Phillips Exeter Academy's century-old summer programme, bringing more than 600 students from over 40 countries and 30 US states to its campus in New Hampshire, an hour north of Boston. Classes use the Harkness method: around a dozen students and a teacher discuss the material at an oval table, so preparation, listening and contributing matter more than grades.

In the Upper School (for students who have completed grades 9–12) students choose three courses across many disciplines, or one of two clusters: the Charles J. Hamm '55 Leadership Program or the Engineering Design Lab. Afternoons bring sports and performing arts, with dorm life, weekend trips and campus events. The 2027 programme runs 5 July to 5 August.

It is a strong option for international students who want an authentic US boarding-school experience and practice in seminar-style learning, which prepares them well for US universities. Need-based aid exists but only for US applicants.
highlights: Harkness discussion classes at a world-famous boarding school
Students from more than 40 countries
Leadership and Engineering Design Lab clusters
exeter-summer-upper-school-2027.eligibility: Students aged 13–18 on 1 September 2027; the Upper School is for those who have completed grades 9–12 (Access Exeter covers grades 7–8). Open to all nationalities; a high level of English is required for discussion classes (non-native speakers with limited English-medium schooling must show proficiency).
how_to_apply: Join an online information session (optional)
Start the application when it opens in early November 2026
Submit the student statements, transcript, teacher recommendation and English evidence if required
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until 10 April 2027; apply early for course choice
US applicants seeking aid file the financial-aid application by 1 March 2027
exeter-summer-upper-school-2027.costs: 2027 Upper School: boarding US$11,500; day US$6,900. Optional extras (rowing US$1,750, soccer or volleyball US$1,100, music lessons US$500). International students must buy the school's health insurance (price TBD). Limited need-based aid for US applicants only; none for international applicants.

andover-summer-session-2027.about:
Andover Summer Session is the summer programme of Phillips Academy, one of the oldest and most selective boarding schools in the United States. Students choose from more than 70 academic courses and intensive institutes across the humanities, sciences, mathematics, computer science and the arts; the Upper School is for rising 9th–12th graders and the Lower School Institute for rising 7th–8th graders.

The 2027 session runs 29 June to 1 August 2027 near Boston. Boarding students live in dorms with peers from around the globe and take part in athletics and activities; add-ons include college counselling, study skills and SAT/PSAT/SSAT preparation, and new for 2027 a L.E.A.D. leadership class.

Tuition for 2027 is US$11,500 (Upper School boarding) plus a US$400 activities fee; day students pay US$3,250–6,500. Andover lists financial-aid information on its tuition page. Students need basic English proficiency (around TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.0 or Duolingo 95–100, though scores need not be submitted).
highlights: 70+ courses and institutes at a top US boarding school
Global student body living on campus for five weeks
Optional college counselling and test prep
andover-summer-session-2027.eligibility: Rising 7th–12th graders (Upper School: rising 9th–12th) from any country. Basic English proficiency needed (about TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.0 or Duolingo 95–100); no ELL courses are offered.
how_to_apply: Browse the 2027 course catalogue
Complete the online application once it opens in November 2026
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis from December, with decisions in 10–14 business days
Apply before February, when popular courses begin to fill
Within two weeks of acceptance pay the 20% deposit; balance due 1 May 2027
andover-summer-session-2027.costs: 2027: Upper School boarding US$11,500; Lower School boarding US$11,700; plus mandatory US$400 activities fee for boarders. Day students US$3,250 (one course) or US$6,500 (two). Optional L.E.A.D. class US$2,700. See the tuition page for financial-aid information.

hotchkiss-summer-portals-2027.about:
Summer Portals is the residential summer programme of The Hotchkiss School, on an 800-acre campus in north-west Connecticut. Each two-week session focuses on one immersive course; most students take two courses and stay four weeks. 2027 offerings include Rocketry, Structural Engineering, Fun with DNA, The Physics of the Electric Guitar, Environmental Science (standard and advanced), Baseball Analytics, Speech and Debate, Writers and Writing, Studio Art, Theatre, a Piano Program and outdoor courses such as climbing and fly fishing.

Afternoons and evenings include sports, swimming, hiking and campus activities; optional add-ons (for a fee) include SSAT prep and a boarding-school application course. The programme has an international student body.

Tuition is all-inclusive of room, board, course expenses and health centre; for example, the 2027 Rocketry course costs US$5,250 per two-week session. It suits younger students (from rising 7th grade) interested in STEM or exploring US boarding schools.
highlights: Hands-on STEM courses like rocketry, DNA science and structural engineering
All-inclusive tuition on an 800-acre campus
Good preparation for US boarding-school applications
hotchkiss-summer-portals-2027.eligibility: Students from rising 7th grade upwards (course-specific age ranges), from any country. Courses are taught in English.
how_to_apply: Browse the 2027 course pages and choose one or two sessions
Complete the online application (open now)
Submit any requested school information
Pay tuition after acceptance; international students arrange a visa if needed
hotchkiss-summer-portals-2027.costs: All-inclusive tuition per two-week course (room, board, course costs, health centre); e.g. Rocketry 2027: US$5,250 per session. Some afternoon options cost extra. No financial-aid details published.

notre-dame-leadership-seminars-2027.about:
Leadership Seminars brings roughly 150 academically talented high-school juniors with impressive community leadership to Notre Dame's campus for ten days. Each student joins one seminar taught by Notre Dame faculty; 2027 topics include AI and Global Business, LEAD-AI, Global Issues: Violence and Peace in the Modern Age, Inequality in America, The American Experiment: Liberty for All?, and The Power of Investing. Seminars combine discussion, readings, service and reflection on what leadership means.

Students may earn one transferable college credit. Session I runs 19–30 June and Session II 10–21 July 2027.

If admitted, the university pays tuition, housing and meals; students cover a US$75 application fee, a US$150 enrolment fee and travel. Admitted students are typically in the top 10% of their class (mid-range SAT 1300–1500 or ACT 31+, though tests are optional). International applicants can apply and must submit TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or PTE results unless they attend an English-medium school.
highlights: Tuition, housing and meals paid by Notre Dame
One transferable college credit
Open to international applicants (English test if needed)
notre-dame-leadership-seminars-2027.eligibility: Current high-school juniors entering senior year in autumn 2027 and planning to go straight to college; at least 16 by 1 August 2027; strong academics (usually top 10%) and demonstrated leadership. International applicants welcome; TOEFL/IELTS/DET/PTE required for those not at English-speaking schools.
how_to_apply: Create an account on Notre Dame's application portal and choose a seminar/session
Enter your counsellor's and a recommending teacher's details (they receive automatic requests)
Write the essays, optionally upload SAT/ACT/PSAT scores (by 31 Jan 2027) and English-test results if international
Pay the US$75 fee and submit by 20 January 2027
If admitted, pay the US$150 enrolment fee by 5 April 2027
notre-dame-leadership-seminars-2027.costs: Tuition, housing and meals are paid by the university. Students pay a US$75 application fee, a US$150 enrolment fee and travel. Fee waivers and travel aid are rare.

notre-dame-summer-scholars-2027.about:
Summer Scholars offers rising juniors and seniors an intensive two-week preview of college academics. Each student takes one small course taught by Notre Dame faculty; 2027 options include Cryptography: From Classical to Quantum-Secure Systems, Engineering and Inventing the Future, Exploring the World of Chemistry, Life Sciences (ecology and cancer biology), Object Design and Prototyping, Climate Change, Law, Psychology, Public Policymaking, Public Speaking and Debate, Film Production, Journalism, Business and Entrepreneurial Immersion.

International students take part through iLED (International Leadership, Enrichment and Development), which adds sessions on leadership, innovation, entrepreneurship and cultural competence, a day of service, and Q&A sessions with Notre Dame admissions. Students may earn one college credit, so international participants need an F-1 visa.

The 2027 cost is US$5,200 in total (US$75 application fee, US$300 enrolment fee and US$4,900 tuition, room and board, activities and field trips). Some donor grants (e.g. KPMG for the Accounting course) can cover programme costs for qualifying students via the Financial Aid Request Form.
highlights: Small college-level courses taught by Notre Dame faculty
iLED strand designed for international students
STEM tracks including cryptography, chemistry and engineering
notre-dame-summer-scholars-2027.eligibility: Current sophomores and juniors (rising juniors and seniors), at least 16 by 1 August 2027, with strong academics. International students welcome (F-1 visa needed); TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo/PTE required if not at an English-speaking school.
how_to_apply: Pick a course and session
Apply online (live since 19 October 2026) with counsellor and teacher contacts
Upload optional test scores by 31 January 2027 and an English test if required
Submit the application and any Financial Aid Request Form by 17 February 2027
If admitted, pay the US$300 enrolment fee by 23 April 2027 and the balance by mid-May
notre-dame-summer-scholars-2027.costs: 2027 total US$5,200: application fee US$75, enrolment fee US$300, tuition/room/board/activities US$4,900. Limited donor-funded grants via the Financial Aid Request Form.

notre-dame-introduction-to-engineering-2.about:
Notre Dame's Introduction to Engineering Program (IEP) has run since the 1990s through the College of Engineering. During two weeks in the summer between junior and senior year, students sample every major branch (aerospace, mechanical, chemical and biomolecular, civil, environmental, electrical, computer engineering, computer science and geological sciences) through informal lectures by faculty and practising engineers, team design projects, programming, lab and facility tours, and field trips.

The 2027 sessions run 20 June–3 July and 11–24 July. Students live in campus dorms, and the programme ends with a banquet for students and families.

The 2027 cost is US$3,350, covering registration, field trips, meals and housing. Partial scholarships can be requested after admission. It is good value for students unsure which engineering major to choose.
highlights: Hands-on tour of all major engineering disciplines
Design projects with faculty and practising engineers
Relatively affordable at US$3,350 all-inclusive; partial scholarships
notre-dame-introduction-to-engineering-2.eligibility: High-school students in the summer between junior and senior year. The site does not state nationality limits; international applicants should confirm with the programme.
how_to_apply: Watch for the application opening in mid-November 2026 on the IEP site
Submit the online application; shortlisted applicants are asked for a transcript
After admission, complete the forms (including any partial-scholarship request) and pay the deposit
notre-dame-introduction-to-engineering-2.costs: 2027: US$3,350 including registration, field trips, meals and dorm housing. Partial scholarships can be requested after admission. Travel extra.

pad-foreign-language-assistants-germany-.about:
The Pädagogischer Austauschdienst (PAD), the exchange service of Germany's Standing Conference of Education Ministers, places up to 800 students from abroad each school year in German schools as foreign language assistants (Fremdsprachenassistenzkräfte). Assistants support teachers in lessons in their native language, improve their German in everyday and school life, and get to know the German education system first-hand.

The exchange rests on bilateral agreements with Australia, Belgium (Wallonia), Canada (anglophone and francophone), France, Ireland, Italy, New Zealand, Spain, Switzerland (francophone), Taiwan, the United Kingdom and the United States; resumption with China is being prepared. The official assistantship runs from 15 September to 31 May (to 30 June for Taiwan and the USA).

It is a paid, low-risk way for language and teaching students to live in Germany for a school year. Applicants apply directly in their home country through the institution PAD lists for each country.
highlights: EUR 1,000 monthly stipend plus insurance
Teach your native language in a German school
Partner countries include the UK, Ireland, France, Italy, Spain, USA and Canada
pad-foreign-language-assistants-germany-.eligibility: University students (often language or teacher-training students) who are nationals of, and apply from, one of the 13 partner countries; exact requirements, including German level, are set by the responsible home-country institution.
how_to_apply: Open the PAD page for students from abroad and pick your country.
Follow the link to the responsible institution in your country and check its requirements and deadline.
Apply through that institution (not directly to PAD).
If selected, PAD assigns you a school; prepare housing, insurance and arrival for 15 September 2027.
pad-foreign-language-assistants-germany-.costs: Monthly stipend of EUR 1,000; health, accident and liability insurance (PAD-PLUS) during the assistantship; assistants can apply for German housing benefit. Travel is usually self-funded.

sacgc-national-bridge-building-competiti.about:
The National Bridge Building Competition, now in its third season, is organised by the Sabah Al-Ahmad Center for Giftedness and Creativity, a centre of the Kuwait Foundation for the Advancement of Sciences (KFAS). Teams apply physics and engineering principles to a real structure: using 200 wooden sticks, they must design and build a bridge model to exact specifications that spans a 40 cm gap and carries the maximum possible load.

The competition takes place on 4–5 December 2026 at the Joint Giftedness Academy (Boys). Day 1 (Friday) is a four-hour build session after a rules briefing. Day 2 (Saturday) includes team presentations and a design display, load testing in two groups and the awards ceremony. Bridges are judged on maximum load relative to the bridge's own weight and the amount of material used (Strength Award: KWD 400, 300 and 200), on innovation, elegance and function (Design Award: KWD 200), and on the team poster explaining the project (Best Poster: KWD 200). Teams may photograph their design process beforehand and complete their poster during the build.

It is a hands-on introduction to structural engineering that builds planning, design, creative thinking, teamwork, decision-making and time-management skills, and gives future engineering applicants a concrete national competition result.
highlights: Build a wooden bridge from 200 sticks to span 40 cm
KWD 1,300 in prizes (strength, design, poster)
Free national competition for grades 9–12
sacgc-national-bridge-building-competiti.eligibility: Kuwaiti high-school students in grades 9–12 from public and private schools, in teams of 2–4 with a supervisor.
how_to_apply: Form a team of two to four students and find a supervising teacher
Register your team on bbc.sacgc.org before 15 November 2026
Practise designs and document your design process with photos
Compete on 4–5 December at the Joint Giftedness Academy (Boys)
sacgc-national-bridge-building-competiti.costs: Free to enter; materials are provided under the competition specifications.

sacgc-stem-racing-for-schools-2026-27.about:
STEM Racing (formerly F1 in Schools) is the world's largest STEM motorsport challenge, supported by Formula 1. In Kuwait it is run by the Sabah Al-Ahmad Center for Giftedness and Creativity (KFAS). For the 2026-27 season, SACGC's team visits schools to introduce students to designing, engineering and racing a scale Formula 1 car and helps them form teams.

The road has four stages: (1) the school books a visit; (2) teams register and progress through design and build checkpoints; (3) teams race their cars at the national competition; and (4) the top two teams represent Kuwait at the international competition in Singapore. Once at least 20 schools register (18 had registered at the time of checking), prizes unlock: a complete manufacturing room for the winning school and USD 5,000 in cash for the winning team, shared between mentor and students. SACGC also runs introductory STEM Racing workshops on aerodynamics using paper cars.

The challenge combines CAD design, aerodynamics, manufacturing, project management, branding and presentation, which makes it excellent preparation for engineering, design and business degrees.
highlights: Design and race a miniature F1 car, supported by Formula 1
Top two teams go to the international final in Singapore
USD 5,000 team prize and a manufacturing room for the winning school (once 20 schools join)
sacgc-stem-racing-for-schools-2026-27.eligibility: Schools in Kuwait; teams of 5–6 students in grades 9–11, aged 14–17 on 1 January 2027, with at least 80% Kuwaiti nationals and a teacher mentor from the registered school. One visit per school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school to book a STEM Racing visit on srs.sacgc.org
Attend the visit and receive your school code
Form a team of 5–6 students with a teacher mentor
Register the team through the link shared after the visit
Pass the design and build checkpoints and race at the national final
sacgc-stem-racing-for-schools-2026-27.costs: Free for schools and students; SACGC provides the visit and competition.

sacgc-acceleration-program-food-water-20.about:
SACGC's Acceleration Program 2026 identifies Kuwaiti innovation addressing food and water security and moves high-potential projects towards validation, pilot readiness, commercialisation and international exposure. It is designed for projects beyond the idea stage, such as prototypes, MVPs, beta solutions or pilots; a registered company is not required. Target sectors include advanced food production, controlled environments, food safety and traceability, supply-chain resilience and alternative food systems, as well as smart irrigation, water reuse, leak detection and conservation technologies.

Stage 1 is the Kuwait Acceleration Sprint (16–23 November 2026): problem framing and validation, customer discovery and lean startup, food and water market insights, MVP development, business models, technical feasibility and pitch training, ending with a Pitch and Selection Day on 23 November. Stage 2 takes the top 10 finalists on an International Mission to Barcelona (8–17 December 2026) delivered with Mind the Bridge, a global open-innovation platform: one-to-one sessions with scaling managers, meetings with AgriTech, desalination and corporate innovation stakeholders, and an International Demo Day on 15 December.

It is open to university students with a capstone project in the field, activists, inventors and entrepreneurs, and is a rare chance for young Gulf innovators to get European ecosystem exposure.
highlights: Week-long acceleration sprint in Kuwait with expert mentors
Top 10 go to Barcelona for an international mission and demo day
Open to students with capstone projects as well as founders
sacgc-acceleration-program-food-water-20.eligibility: Kuwaiti nationals aged 21–35 with an MVP or beta-stage solution relevant to food or water security (software, hardware, web or AI solutions prioritised), fluent English, and able to obtain a US/Schengen visa. University students with a related capstone project, activists, inventors and entrepreneurs may apply.
how_to_apply: Read the programme terms on acceleration.sacgc.org
Submit the online application form before 12 November 2026
If selected, attend the full Kuwait sprint (16–23 November)
Pitch on 23 November; the top 10 prepare visas for Barcelona
sacgc-acceleration-program-food-water-20.costs: No participation fee is listed on the official site; finalists must obtain their own visa. Confirm travel coverage with SACGC.

sacgc-harvard-pre-college-scholarship-20.about:
Through its Global Enrichment Program, the Sabah Al-Ahmad Center for Giftedness and Creativity (a KFAS centre) supports five Kuwaiti students to attend the Harvard Summer School Pre-College Program in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The programme offers two weeks of university-level academic exploration and discussion with students from around the world. Summer 2027 sessions run 21 June–2 July, 12–23 July and 26 July–6 August. Only STEM modules qualify for SACGC funding.

The process: apply directly to Harvard Summer School and obtain an unconditional acceptance; email the letter to SACGC for scholarship consideration and an interview; pay a non-refundable KWD 250 administrative fee to reserve the place; the parent pays Harvard and books the approved flight; then SACGC reimburses approved programme fees and round-trip economy airfare by bank transfer in the first week of the programme, after verifying enrolment. Families pay for health insurance and any visa.

The programme aims to help gifted students discover their capabilities, build research skills, gain cross-cultural experience and prepare for admission to leading universities.
highlights: Five funded places for Kuwaiti students
Two-week STEM module at Harvard Summer School
Programme fees and economy airfare reimbursed
sacgc-harvard-pre-college-scholarship-20.eligibility: Kuwaiti nationals at least 16 years old by 20 June 2026 and not turning 19 before 31 July 2027; GPA of 95% or equivalent; demonstrated English proficiency; documented STEM competitions, research or projects; a successful SACGC interview; no previous SACGC international trip or enrichment programme.
how_to_apply: Attend Harvard Summer School's virtual session (17 Nov 2026) and apply to a STEM module of the Pre-College Program
Obtain an unconditional acceptance letter
Submit the letter and documents to SACGC via its enrichment-programs form and attend the interview
Pay the KWD 250 administrative fee after approval
Pay Harvard, book the approved flight and claim reimbursement
sacgc-harvard-pre-college-scholarship-20.costs: SACGC reimburses approved programme fees and round-trip economy airfare. Families pay a non-refundable KWD 250 administrative fee, health insurance and visa costs, and must pay upfront before reimbursement.

sacgc-yale-young-global-scholars-scholar.about:
Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS) is a two-week residential academic programme at Yale University in New Haven for outstanding high-school students from around the world. Through its Global Enrichment Program, the Sabah Al-Ahmad Center for Giftedness and Creativity supports Kuwaiti students who are admitted to the Innovations in Science and Technology (IST) session, where they explore STEM topics, exchange ideas with peers from many countries and experience university-level learning. Summer 2027 sessions run 20 June–2 July, 4–16 July and 18–30 July.

The journey: attend a SACGC virtual information session (5 or 12 November 2026, 7–8 pm Kuwait time); apply to YYGS for the IST session by 6 January 2027; obtain an unconditional YYGS offer; submit it to SACGC for scholarship consideration and interview; confirm the place; then pay, book flights and attend. SACGC reimburses approved programme fees and economy airfare in the first week of the programme. A KWD 250 administrative fee applies, and families cover health insurance and visa. Students should wait for SACGC confirmation before paying anything.

YYGS is one of the most respected summer programmes for international students, and SACGC funding makes it accessible to high-achieving Kuwaiti students.
highlights: Funded place at Yale Young Global Scholars (STEM session)
Two weeks residential at Yale with students from around the world
SACGC info sessions on 5 and 12 November 2026
sacgc-yale-young-global-scholars-scholar.eligibility: Kuwaiti students who will be 16–18 by August 2027, with a GPA of 95% or equivalent, demonstrated English proficiency, documented STEM projects, research or competitions, a successful SACGC interview, and no previous SACGC international trip or enrichment programme.
how_to_apply: Register for a SACGC virtual session (5 or 12 November 2026)
Apply to YYGS for the Innovations in Science and Technology session by 6 January 2027
Obtain an unconditional YYGS acceptance
Submit it to SACGC through the enrichment-programs form and pass the interview
After SACGC confirms, pay the KWD 250 fee, pay Yale, book flights and claim reimbursement
sacgc-yale-young-global-scholars-scholar.costs: SACGC reimburses approved YYGS fees and round-trip economy airfare. Families pay a non-refundable KWD 250 administrative fee, health insurance and visa costs, and pay upfront before reimbursement.

kuwait-red-crescent-youth-volunteering.about:
The Kuwait Red Crescent Society (KRCS) treats volunteering as a fundamental pillar of its humanitarian mission. It recruits volunteers of all ages and especially seeks to increase youth participation, offering a motivating environment with structured programmes and specialised courses.

Volunteers are trained in first aid, disaster management and community services, and support KRCS relief programmes and campaigns in Kuwait and abroad. KRCS also runs public first-aid courses and a youth group, which can be contacted directly.

Volunteering with a national Red Crescent society builds practical emergency skills, teamwork and a record of sustained community service that is valued by universities and scholarship committees, particularly for students interested in medicine, public health or international affairs.
highlights: Training in first aid and disaster management
Local and international humanitarian campaigns
Rolling sign-up with a youth group
kuwait-red-crescent-youth-volunteering.eligibility: Residents of Kuwait of any age (the form asks for age); a special focus on young people. Some activities may have minimum ages.
how_to_apply: Open the 'Volunteer With Us' page on krcs.org.kw
Fill in the form (name, email, mobile, age, gender)
Wait for the KRCS youth team to contact you
Attend orientation and training before activities

qstp-agritech-accelerator-2027.about:
The QSTP AgriTech Accelerator is one of Qatar Science & Technology Park's sector accelerators, alongside its FemTech (with Merck) and WaterTech (with TotalEnergies) programmes. It targets purpose-driven startups building technology for food security, sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation and disaster management, areas of national priority for a country that imports most of its food.

Over three months in a hybrid format (in person in Doha and virtual), founders refine their technology, test their concepts in real-world conditions such as Qatar's farms and arid climate, and connect with industry partners, potential customers and investors. The programme offers mentorship, market access and pilot opportunities, plus visibility within QSTP's ecosystem, including its $30 million Tech Venture Fund for Qatar-based deep-tech startups.

It suits growth-ready founders, including university spin-outs and student teams with a working prototype, who want to prove their impact in one of the world's harshest agricultural environments.
highlights: Pilots in real Qatari conditions
Mentoring, market access and investor visibility
Hybrid format; no programme fee stated
qstp-agritech-accelerator-2027.eligibility: Startups and founders working on agritech, food security, climate and sustainability solutions, ready to test and scale; regional founders welcome.
how_to_apply: Read the AgriTech Accelerator page on qstp.qa
Submit the register-your-interest form
Complete the full application when the cohort call opens
Join the three-month programme if selected

doha-film-festival-2026-festival-accredi.about:
The Doha Film Festival, organised by the Doha Film Institute, runs from 19 to 27 November 2026 at Katara Cultural Village and other venues in Doha, bringing together Arab and international cinema, filmmakers and the region's creative community. It includes the Ajyal youth juries and the Doha Industry Days.

Festival Accreditation is designed for film lovers and members of the creative community. It gives access to screenings and talks, free or discounted tickets to selected Music Programme events and a festival bag. Industry Accreditation (for professionals) adds Doha Industry Days, the DFF Majlis with meals and a listing in the industry directory. Places are limited and every application is personally reviewed.

For university students in film, media, journalism or the arts, accreditation is a direct way to watch new regional cinema, hear directors in talks and network with professionals at one of the Middle East's leading film events.
highlights: Screenings and talks across the festival
Discounted music programme tickets
Networking with the regional film community
doha-film-festival-2026-festival-accredi.eligibility: Film lovers, creative-community members and film professionals; applications are individually reviewed. Under-18s should consider DFI's Ajyal youth programmes instead.
how_to_apply: Open the Doha Film Festival accreditation page on dohafilm.com
Choose Festival or Industry Accreditation and complete the online application
Apply before 2 November for early-bird pricing, or before 19 November 2026 at the latest
Pay the accreditation fee after approval and collect your badge
doha-film-festival-2026-festival-accredi.costs: Paid accreditation with early-bird pricing until 2 November 2026; prices are shown on the official page.

hbkux-online-courses-edx.about:
HBKUx is Hamad Bin Khalifa University's online learning programme on edX. HBKU, a Qatar Foundation university in Education City, publishes courses based on its research strengths, so learners anywhere can study Qatar-specific expertise without enrolling.

The catalogue currently has 12 courses: Applications of AI in Healthcare; Precision Medicine: From Genomics to Clinical Decisions; Islamic Bioethics; Solar Resource Assessment in Desert Climates; Using Photovoltaic Technology in Desert Climates; Education for Sustainable Development; Navigating Peace Education in Times of Conflict; International Charities in Humanitarian Crises; Navigating Legal and Commercial Aspects of Sports; two courses on Sustainability and Major Sport Events (principles and implementation, drawing on Qatar's FIFA World Cup experience); and Comparative Social Theory and Methods. Three two-course Professional Certificates bundle the solar, education-for-peace and sport-sustainability courses.

All courses can be audited for free, or learners can pay a small fee for a verified certificate. They are a good way for high school and university students to explore a field before choosing a major, add a university-branded certificate to a CV, or prepare for HBKU's graduate programmes.
highlights: Free to audit, open worldwide
Topics from AI in healthcare to desert solar energy
Optional verified certificates and 3 professional certificates
hbkux-online-courses-edx.eligibility: Anyone with an edX account; no admission requirements. Courses are in English.
how_to_apply: Open the HBKUx page on edX
Choose a course and click Enrol
Select the free audit track or pay for a verified certificate
Study at the pace set by the course run
hbkux-online-courses-edx.costs: Free to audit; verified certificates for a small fee set by edX.

ucd-global-excellence-scholarship-underg.about:
University College Dublin is Ireland's largest and most international university, ranked in the world top 150 and known for business, engineering, agriculture and veterinary science, computer science and social sciences. Each year its Global Excellence Scholarships give a limited number of 100% and 50% tuition-fee awards to outstanding international students on non-EU fees starting undergraduate or taught master's programmes in September.

UCD has confirmed the 2027/28 round will open in November 2026, with terms and eligible programmes published then. Deadlines are regional; in the last round undergraduates from North America applied by 1 February, from the Middle East, Africa and Pakistan by 28 February, and from all other regions by 31 March. Results come about seven weeks after each deadline via SISWeb. Apply to your programme early, as decisions can take longer in peak periods.
highlights: 100% or 50% of non-EU tuition
Regional deadlines Feb–Mar 2027 (round opens Nov 2026)
Results about 7 weeks after each deadline
ucd-global-excellence-scholarship-underg.eligibility: Outstanding international applicants on non-EU fees applying to an eligible UCD undergraduate programme starting September 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply to your UCD undergraduate programme (non-EU route) as early as possible
When the 2027/28 round opens in November 2026, read the eligible programmes and instructions
Submit the Global Excellence Scholarship application through SISWeb by your regional deadline
Check SISWeb for results about seven weeks later
ucd-global-excellence-scholarship-underg.costs: Covers 100% or 50% of non-EU tuition (UCD undergraduate non-EU fees are roughly €22,000–€30,000+ a year). Living costs in Dublin (about €1,200–1,800/month) are not covered.

trinity-global-excellence-undergraduate-.about:
Trinity College Dublin, Ireland's oldest and highest-ranked university, offers Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarships to new non-EU fee-paying students. The award is worth €2,000 to €5,000 depending on region, applied as a reduction of first-year tuition.

You need an offer for year one of a full-time undergraduate degree. Some programmes are excluded (medicine, dentistry, acting, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics) and Chinese students apply instead for the Claddagh Scholarship. The short online form asks for your personal details, school results and a statement on how you will contribute to the Trinity community. Early application is advised.
highlights: €2,000–€5,000 off first-year tuition
Short online form with a contribution statement
Regional deadlines from April to July
trinity-global-excellence-undergraduate-.eligibility: New students with non-EU fee status holding an offer for year one of a full-time Trinity undergraduate degree (excluding medicine, dentistry, acting, engineering, natural sciences, computer science and statistics). Not for students from China.
how_to_apply: Apply to Trinity (non-EU route) and receive an offer
Complete the online Global Excellence application form
Submit by your regional deadline (expected 1 April–15 July 2027)
trinity-global-excellence-undergraduate-.costs: One-off €2,000–€5,000 off first-year tuition (non-EU tuition about €20,000–€30,000+).

exeter-excellence-scholarship-undergradu.about:
The University of Exeter, a Russell Group university in south-west England known for business, economics, environmental science, law and the humanities, offers 150 Exeter Excellence Scholarships to international undergraduates for 2027/28. Each is a recurring £15,000 tuition-fee discount for every eligible year of study.

You need international fee status (including EU students paying international fees), an offer to enter year one in September 2027, and grades at or predicted at AAB at A-level or equivalent. Recipients must be self-funded and cannot combine it with another Exeter scholarship. The application is a short webform with a 300-word personal statement in two parts: your aspirations and how you will contribute to the university. Medicine, diagnostic radiography and a few partnership programmes are excluded.
highlights: £15,000 off tuition every year
150 awards for 2027 entry
Round 1 closes 4 March 2027; results by 6 April
exeter-excellence-scholarship-undergradu.eligibility: International fee-status applicants (incl. EU students paying international fees) with an offer to start year one of an eligible Exeter undergraduate degree in September 2027, expected to achieve AAB or equivalent, self-funded. Excludes BMBS Medicine, Diagnostic Radiography, some partnership law degrees, apprenticeships and International Study Centre progression.
how_to_apply: Apply to Exeter via UCAS (deadline 13 January 2027 for equal consideration)
Receive a conditional or unconditional offer
Complete the scholarship webform with two 150-word answers
Submit before 11:59 GMT on 4 March 2027; results by 6 April 2027
exeter-excellence-scholarship-undergradu.costs: £15,000 off tuition each year. Exeter overseas tuition is about £25,000–£31,000 a year; living costs are not covered.

sheffield-international-undergraduate-sc.about:
The University of Sheffield, a Russell Group university strong in engineering, architecture, computer science and the life sciences, gives every eligible self-funded international undergraduate starting in September 2027 a £2,500 tuition discount for each year of study, up to £10,000 for a four-year degree. Later years require a 60% average.

There is no application form: you are eligible if you hold overseas fee status, study full-time on campus and choose Sheffield as your firm or insurance UCAS choice by 4pm UK time on 2 June 2027. deutschlandstipendium-2027.about:
The Deutschlandstipendium is Germany's national merit scholarship. It pays €300 a month: €150 from a business, foundation or private sponsor, matched by €150 from the federal government. Students of all nationalities at public and state-recognised universities can apply, including those just starting their first semester. In 2022 around 30,500 students received it.

Selection is by each university and looks at grades and academic potential, social commitment and personal achievements such as overcoming obstacles in your background. Your income and that of your parents play no role. Many sponsors add mentoring, networking or internships. Because most German public universities charge little or no tuition, €300 a month makes a real contribution to living costs. Apply through the university where you enrol, by its own deadline.

yc-startup-school.about:

Lessons cover planning an MVP, modern startup funding (from the inventor of the SAFE), launching in the press, getting users and growing, leading teams and how and when to apply to YC, plus founder stories from Facebook, 23andMe, Boom and others. It takes roughly seven weeks at one to two hours a week.

Members also get a weekly update tool to stay accountable and access to YC Co-Founder Matching, the world's largest co-founder matching platform with more than 100,000 matches: you create a profile, see recommended candidates by skills, interests and location, and invite people to explore working together.

It is the best free starting point for any student curious about founding a company, and good preparation before applying to YC, Z Fellows or other accelerators.

entrepreneurship-world-cup-2027.about:

It is open to startups at every stage: Idea (concept or prototype), Early (product in market, early revenue) and Growth (scaling), plus Artificial Intelligence sub-tracks.

Prizes are 100% equity-free; the 2026 pool included $200,000 for the early-stage grand prize, $160,000 for growth, $30,000 for idea stage and $50,000 for each AI sub-track. Finalists also get investor access and soft-landing support in Saudi Arabia and the MENA region.

robocupjunior-2027-nuremberg.about:

Teams qualify through their own region's events: talk to your Regional Representative about qualifying competitions, and see RoboCupJunior's 'Qualification and Competitions' page; there is still time to start a team this season.

stockholm-junior-water-prize-2027.about:
The Stockholm Junior Water Prize (SJWP) is an international competition for students aged 15 to 20 who develop innovative research projects addressing major water challenges: water quality and treatment, scarcity, sanitation, microplastics, ecosystems or water-related technology. It has been held annually since 1997 and attracts tens of thousands of participants from around 40 countries.

Students first compete in their national SJWP competition (often run by a water association, science-fair body or ministry). National winners travel to Stockholm for the international final during World Water Week, where a jury of international water experts evaluates their projects and the prize is presented by the patron, H.R.H. Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden. Finalists also join a global alumni community, and the 2026 prize went to a Canadian student's robot that removes plastic from water while sparing marine life.

It is an outstanding goal for students doing environmental or engineering research, and national rounds often double as science-fair qualifiers.

world-scholars-cup-2026-27.about:

Teams of three study a yearly theme spanning science and technology, social studies, history, literature and a special area, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (individual multiple-choice) and the Scholar's Bowl (team quiz). Schools can field unlimited teams.

The season starts with regional rounds in more than 100 cities worldwide (for 2026–27 these began in late October 2026, e.g. Al Ain, Kuwait, Haikou and Dalian). Qualifying teams advance to Global Rounds (for example a Tokyo-Yokohama Global Round on 11–15 December 2026) and then to the Tournament of Champions at Yale University; the 2026 Tournament of Champions took place on 12–18 November 2026. The calendar for the rest of the season is being posted over the coming weeks.

WSC is famous for being welcoming and fun (medals for many participants, a 'Scholar's Ball'), while building debate, writing and research skills. It is especially popular in Asia, the Middle East and Australia.

hkmun-2027.about:
Hong Kong Model United Nations is a student-run high-school conference that has grown into the city's largest MUN, attracting local and international schools.

The conference runs 19–21 March 2027 in Hong Kong, Hong Kong at Hong Kong Science & Technology Park and is aimed at high school students. Working language: English. Committees and topics are published on the official website before the conference.

Schools and individual delegates register via the forms linked from the official site. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.
highlights: 3 days (19–21 March 2027) in Hong Kong, Hong Kong
For high school students
General Assembly, Security Council and specialised committees
hkmun-2027.eligibility: Open to high school students of any nationality, usually registering as a school delegation with a faculty advisor. Working language: English.

seamun-i-2027.about:
SEAMUN I offers ten committees, including a fantasy committee and a press corps, plus digital note-passing and a personal delegate dashboard. The organisers donate 100% of any surplus to the Thai Red Cross Society.

The conference runs 16–17 January 2027 in Bangkok, Thailand at D-PREP International School, Secondary Campus (Bang Phli, Samut Prakan, Greater Bangkok) and is aimed at high school and university students. Working language: English. Committees: DISEC, ECOSOC, UNHRC, UNODC, UNSC, UN Women, WHO, INTERPOL, a fantasy committee and press.

Independent delegates, advisors and chairs register through the forms page; capacity is limited to 200 delegates. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.

Surplus donated to the Thai Red Cross
Committees: DISEC, ECOSOC, UNHRC, UNODC, UNSC, UN Women, WHO, INTERPOL, a fantasy committee and press
