sacgc-technology-capacity-building-clubs.about:
The Technology Capacity Building (TCB) clubs are run by the Sabah Al-Ahmad Center for Giftedness and Creativity, a centre of the Kuwait Foundation for the Advancement of Sciences. They offer short, hands-on technology courses at the Joint Giftedness Academy in Al-Sawaber (Kuwait City) and at science clubs in Al-Jahra and Al-Ahmadi, plus STEM Racing sessions at The Avenues mall.

The November 2026 schedule at Al-Sawaber alone lists about 25 courses, each running two or three weekday evenings (5–7 pm): Cubroid and Matata coding robots and electronic circuits for ages 6–10; cybersecurity basics and online ethics; an introduction to AI and machine learning; 3D design for 3D printing; Laser Makers; 'Design Your Website Using AI' and 3D modelling in Blender for ages 11–14; and Fischertechnik robotics and mechatronics for ages 9–13. Classes are small (around 8–13 seats) and taught mainly in Arabic.

At KWD 2 per course they are an easy, affordable way for younger students to try different areas of technology before committing to competitions such as WRO or STEM Racing.
highlights: Robotics, coding, AI, cybersecurity, electronics and 3D design
KWD 2 per course, small classes
Clubs in Kuwait City, Al-Jahra and Al-Ahmadi
sacgc-technology-capacity-building-clubs.eligibility: Children and young teens aged 6–14 (each course lists its own age band) who can attend in person in Kuwait. Courses are mostly taught in Arabic.
how_to_apply: Open tcbclubs.sacgc.org and choose a location
Pick a course that matches your age and dates
Sign in and click 'Enroll Now' while seats are available
Attend all sessions of the course

sydney-international-undergraduate-acade.about:
The University of Sydney, Australia's oldest university and a member of the Group of Eight, offers the Sydney International Undergraduate Academic Excellence Scholarship to high-achieving international school leavers. It covers 100% of tuition fees and the Student Services and Amenities Fee (SSAF) for the published full-time duration of a single undergraduate degree (up to four years, including embedded honours).

About 20 scholarships are awarded globally each year across the February and July intakes, with a focus on diversity of course and nationality. Applications for Semester 1 2027 have closed, but applications are welcome for students commencing in Semester 2 (July) 2027. You must have applied for (but not started) an eligible single undergraduate degree, have finished secondary school or an approved foundation programme, and have no previous tertiary study.

Recipients pay their own living costs, accommodation, Overseas Student Health Cover, textbooks and flights. Only successful applicants are contacted.
highlights: 100% tuition + SSAF for the whole degree
About 20 awards a year worldwide
Open now for July 2027 entry
sydney-international-undergraduate-acade.eligibility: International students (not Australian citizens/PRs or dual Australians) who have completed secondary school or an approved foundation programme, have applied for an eligible single undergraduate degree of up to four years starting Semester 2 2027, and have not undertaken tertiary study.
how_to_apply: Apply to the University of Sydney for an eligible bachelor's degree starting Semester 2, 2027
Submit the scholarship application through the scholarship page while it is open
Wait to be contacted (only successful applicants are notified)
Enrol full-time to activate the award
sydney-international-undergraduate-acade.costs: 100% of tuition fees and SSAF for the standard full-time duration; living costs, accommodation, OSHC, books and flights not covered.

sydney-vice-chancellors-international-sc.about:
The Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships Scheme (VCIS) supports high-achieving international students starting a coursework degree (including bachelor's degrees) at the University of Sydney. It is paid once, in the first year: depending on your ranking you can receive A$60,000 or A$40,000 (paid over two semesters), or A$20,000, A$10,000 or A$5,000 (paid for one semester). It is not renewable.

No application is needed: every eligible student who holds an unconditional offer of admission by a round's closing date is automatically considered, subject to funding. For Semester 1 (February) 2027 the last regular round closes on 16 November 2026, with extra offer rounds for IB graduates after the December results and for international UAC students after the 23 December offer round. For Semester 2 (July) 2027 the rounds close on 15 February, 22 March and 3 May 2027.
highlights: Up to A$60,000 in the first year
Automatic with an unconditional offer
Several rounds through May 2027
sydney-vice-chancellors-international-sc.eligibility: International students applying for a CRICOS-registered coursework degree at the University of Sydney who receive an unconditional offer of admission by the relevant round's closing date.
how_to_apply: Apply to the University of Sydney and secure an unconditional offer before a round closes
No scholarship form needed: eligible students are considered automatically
Successful students are told the award amount (A$5,000–60,000)
sydney-vice-chancellors-international-sc.costs: One-off first-year award of A$60,000, A$40,000, A$20,000, A$10,000 or A$5,000; not renewable.

kyoto-iup-international-undergraduate-pr.about:
Kyoto University, one of Asia's most prestigious research universities, runs the Kyoto International Undergraduate Program (Kyoto iUP) to bring talented international students into its regular faculties. Students start with a six-month preparatory course (intensive Japanese and academic preparation) and then complete a four-year bachelor's degree in one of nine faculties: Integrated Human Studies, Letters, Education, Law, Economics, Science, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering or Agriculture.

Funding is built in: every Kyoto iUP student receives a full admission-fee waiver and full or partial tuition waivers for four and a half years, plus a monthly allowance of up to JPY 120,000 during the preparatory course. After entering the undergraduate course, merit-based monthly allowances from supporting companies and organisations are available to eligible students.

There are 40 places for October 2027 enrolment. Applications are made through the online system between 2 November and 3 December 2026 (5 pm Japan time).
highlights: Admission-fee waiver + full/partial tuition waiver for 4.5 years
Up to JPY 120,000/month during the 6-month prep course
40 places in nine Kyoto University faculties
kyoto-iup-international-undergraduate-pr.eligibility: International students who have completed (or will complete) secondary education and meet the academic and language requirements in the Kyoto iUP October 2027 Application Guidelines.
how_to_apply: Read the Kyoto iUP Application Guidelines for October 2027 enrolment
Choose your faculty (one of nine)
Submit the online application and documents between 2 Nov and 3 Dec 2026 (5 pm JST)
Complete any further selection steps announced in the guidelines
kyoto-iup-international-undergraduate-pr.costs: Full admission-fee waiver, full or partial tuition waivers for 4.5 years, up to JPY 120,000/month in the prep course; merit allowances from sponsors afterwards for eligible students.

gist-international-undergraduate-scholar.about:
The Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (GIST) is a research-intensive science and engineering institute in southwest Korea, with a small undergraduate college (GIST College) focused on the natural sciences and engineering.

International undergraduates receive a full tuition waiver for eight semesters with no conditions, a settlement subsidy of KRW 200,000 and reimbursement of a one-way flight after their first month. Monthly support includes a student allowance of KRW 130,000 and a meal allowance of KRW 270,000 (for students with at least 11 credits and no probation), plus an international allowance of KRW 130,000 for students who keep a good GPA.

The 2027 application period runs from 1 December 2026 to 29 January 2027 (Korea time) on GIST's online admission system.
highlights: Tuition fully waived for 8 semesters
Monthly allowances (~KRW 400,000–530,000) plus settlement grant
STEM degree at a Korean research institute
gist-international-undergraduate-scholar.eligibility: International applicants (non-Korean nationality as defined in the 2027 GIST guidelines) who have completed or will complete secondary school, with strong maths and science preparation and English proficiency.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 GIST Undergraduate Admission Guidelines for International Applicants
Prepare transcripts, recommendation letters, essays and English scores
Apply online at service.gist.ac.kr between 1 Dec 2026 and 29 Jan 2027
Take part in the interview stage if shortlisted
gist-international-undergraduate-scholar.costs: Full tuition waiver (8 semesters); KRW 130,000 student + KRW 270,000 meal + KRW 130,000 international allowance per month (conditions apply); KRW 200,000 settlement subsidy; one-way flight.

ilspsd-erasmus-mundus-2027.about:
ILSPSD is a 24-month Erasmus Mundus Joint Master run by Leuphana University of Lüneburg (Germany), the Institut Barcelona d'Estudis Internacionals (Spain), the University of Glasgow (UK), Université libre de Bruxelles (Belgium), Universidade NOVA de Lisboa (Portugal) and the University of Tartu (Estonia), with 30 associate partners. Students start in Lüneburg, continue in Barcelona and then choose one of four specialisation tracks, studying in at least three countries.

It covers international law on armed conflict, peace-building, human rights, security and sustainable development, preparing graduates for international organisations, NGOs, governments and research. An LLM track needs 60 ECTS in law; the MA track accepts law, political science, international relations or European studies. English at C1 (IELTS 7.0) is required; the Brussels track also needs French B2.

The second intake (2027–2029) starts in October 2027. EMJM scholarship applicants must apply by 4 January 2027 and must already have finished their degree; scholarships follow the EU standard of €1,400 a month plus full participation costs. Self-funded applicants can apply until 31 March 2027.
highlights: Study in at least three of six countries
EMJM scholarships: participation costs + €1,400/month
Scholarship deadline 4 January 2027
ilspsd-erasmus-mundus-2027.eligibility: Any nationality. Undergraduate degree of at least 180 ECTS (completed by the deadline for scholarship applicants); for the LLM track 60 ECTS in law, for the MA track 60 ECTS in law, political science, IR or European studies; track-specific rules for Glasgow, Brussels and Tartu. English CEFR C1 (IELTS Academic 7.0, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1/C2) unless exempt.
how_to_apply: Read the step-by-step application guide and entry requirements
Prepare diploma, transcripts (with ECTS conversion if needed) and English test
Apply through the ILSPSD scholarship application platform (Leuphana)
Submit by 4 January 2027, 23:59 CET for scholarship consideration
ilspsd-erasmus-mundus-2027.costs: EMJM scholarship holders receive coverage of participation costs plus a monthly allowance (EU standard €1,400 per month for 24 months). Self-funded fees are listed on the programme's tuition fees page.

steps-erasmus-mundus-2027.about:
STEPS (Sustainable Transportation and Electric Power Systems) is a 120 ECTS Erasmus Mundus Joint Master led by the University of Oviedo (Spain) with Kiel University (Germany), Sapienza University of Rome (Italy) and the Polytechnic Institute of Coimbra (Portugal), supported by 13 other universities and 24 energy and transport companies.

Students follow either the Coimbra–Kiel–Oviedo or the Rome–Kiel–Oviedo route and choose a Sustainable Transportation or Electrical Power Systems track, covering electric vehicles, power electronics, smart grids and renewable integration. It suits electrical, electronic or energy engineering graduates.

The call for the September 2027 intake is open until 8 January 2027. Erasmus Mundus scholarships give either a full scholarship (tuition plus €1,400 a month for up to 24 months) or a tuition waiver alone; no more than two scholarship holders can share a nationality.
highlights: Study in at least three countries with industry partners
Full scholarship: tuition + €1,400/month for 24 months
Deadline 8 January 2027
steps-erasmus-mundus-2027.eligibility: Any nationality. Bachelor's in electrical, electronic, energy or a related engineering field; English proficiency; full-time study. Partner-country applicants must not have lived in an Erasmus+ programme country for more than 12 months in the last five years to count as partner-country students.
how_to_apply: Check the admission page and the two mobility routes
Prepare degree, transcripts, English certificate, CV and letters
Submit the online application by 8 January 2027
Contact info-emmcsteps.eu@uniovi.es for questions
steps-erasmus-mundus-2027.costs: Full scholarship: tuition fees plus €1,400 per month for up to 24 months; or tuition-fee waiver only. Self-funded fees are on the programme's tuition fees page.

radmep-plus-erasmus-mundus-2027.about:
RADMEP+ is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master on the interactions between radiation, microelectronics and photonics, key technologies for space, nuclear, medical and particle-physics environments. Partners are the University of Jyväskylä (Finland), KU Leuven, Ghent University and Vrije Universiteit Brussel (Belgium), and Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne and the University of Montpellier (France), with industry and research associates.

It suits physics, electronics, photonics and engineering graduates who want careers in radiation-hardened electronics, space systems or research (many graduates continue to PhDs).

The 2027–2029 call runs from 16 October 2026 to 9 February 2027 (12:00 UTC); shortlists are announced from mid-February and final results on 22 March 2027, with induction in Jyväskylä at the end of August 2027. EMJM scholarships pay up to €1,400 a month for two years (up to €33,600) plus 100% fee waivers, with around 70 scholarships across the next four intakes.
highlights: Physics and engineering across Finland, Belgium and France
EMJM scholarship up to €33,600 + 100% fee waiver
Deadline 9 February 2027
radmep-plus-erasmus-mundus-2027.eligibility: Any nationality. Bachelor's in physics, electronics, photonics, electrical engineering or related fields, and English proficiency, as listed on the eligibility page. EU geographical-distribution rules apply to scholarships.
how_to_apply: Check the eligibility and how-to-apply pages
Prepare transcripts, diploma, CV, motivation letter, English proof and references
Submit the online application between 16 October 2026 and 9 February 2027
Shortlisted candidates are contacted between 15 February and 15 March 2027
radmep-plus-erasmus-mundus-2027.costs: EMJM scholarship: up to €1,400 per month for 2 years (total up to €33,600) plus 100% fee waiver. RADMEP+ fee waivers reduce tuition for other selected students.

maisi-erasmus-mundus-2027.about:
MAiSI (Master of Arts in Sports Ethics and Integrity) is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master. Semester 1 is at KU Leuven (Belgium), semester 2 at Charles University in Prague with a summer school at the University of Peloponnese in Olympia, semester 3 at Universitat Pompeu Fabra (Barcelona) or Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz depending on the year, and the thesis semester with any partner, ending with a final Olympia summer school.

It covers anti-doping, match-fixing, safeguarding, governance and human rights in sport, and suits graduates of sport science, philosophy, law, social sciences or management aiming at sports federations, anti-doping agencies, NGOs or policy roles.

Applications opened on 8 October 2026. Erasmus Mundus scholarship applicants must apply by 1 February; self-funded non-EEA applicants by 1 April and EEA citizens by 1 July. Scholarships follow the EU standard of €1,400 a month plus participation costs.
highlights: Leuven, Prague, Barcelona/Mainz and Olympia
Erasmus Mundus scholarships for all nationalities
Scholarship deadline 1 February 2027
maisi-erasmus-mundus-2027.eligibility: Any nationality. A relevant bachelor's degree and English proficiency per KU Leuven's admission requirements for MAiSI.
how_to_apply: Read the admission requirements on the MAiSI / KU Leuven pages
Prepare transcripts, CV, motivation letter and references
Apply through the KU Leuven online application and request scholarship consideration
Submit by 1 February 2027
maisi-erasmus-mundus-2027.costs: Erasmus Mundus scholars receive participation-cost coverage and a monthly allowance (EU standard €1,400 for up to 24 months). Self-funded fees are on the Funding Options page.

zonta-amelia-earhart-fellowship-2027.about:
The Amelia Earhart Fellowship, created by Zonta International in 1938 in honour of the aviator, supports women pursuing doctoral degrees in aerospace engineering and space sciences. Up to 30 fellows are chosen each year, and the award can be used at any accredited university in any country.

Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a PhD programme and have completed at least one year of it, or already hold a master's in an aerospace-applied field, and must not graduate before April 2028. Selection rests on academic record, research relevance to aerospace and recommendations.

The 2027 application must be completed online by 15 November 2026, and applicants hear back by the end of April 2027. Alumnae include astronauts, engineers and senior space-agency leaders, which makes it one of the most respected awards for women in the field.
highlights: US$12,000 for women PhD students in aerospace or space science
Use at any university worldwide; up to 30 fellows a year
Deadline 15 November 2026
zonta-amelia-earhart-fellowship-2027.eligibility: Women of any nationality enrolled full-time in a PhD/doctoral programme in aerospace engineering or space sciences (or a closely applied field) who have completed at least one year of the PhD or hold a master's in an aerospace-applied field, with a superior academic record, and who will not graduate before April 2028. Postdocs, Zonta members/employees and previous fellows are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Create an account on Zonta's AwardSpring portal
Write the research and career essays and upload transcripts
Arrange recommendation letters and university verification
Submit the full application by 15 November 2026
zonta-amelia-earhart-fellowship-2027.costs: A one-off US$12,000 fellowship for the academic year, usable for tuition, living or research costs.

peo-international-peace-scholarship-2027.about:
The P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship Fund, set up in 1949 by the P.E.O. Sisterhood, gives grants to women from other countries for graduate study in the United States and Canada, in the belief that education builds world peace and understanding.

Awards of up to US$12,500 go to women enrolled (or admitted) in full-time master's or doctoral programmes at accredited US or Canadian institutions who plan to return to their home country after graduating. It is a supplementary award, so most recipients combine it with university funding or other scholarships.

The online eligibility form and application open each autumn, and applications are accepted through 15 December for the following academic year.
highlights: Up to US$12,500 for graduate study in the US or Canada
For women from outside the US and Canada
Deadline 15 December 2026
peo-international-peace-scholarship-2027.eligibility: Women who are not US or Canadian citizens or permanent residents, enrolled or admitted to full-time graduate study (master's or doctorate) at an accredited college or university in the US or Canada, who intend to return home after their studies. International students at Cottey College are also eligible.
how_to_apply: Open the IPS form on the P.E.O. International website
Complete the eligibility questions
If eligible, fill in the full application with financial information and references
Submit by 15 December 2026
peo-international-peace-scholarship-2027.costs: Up to US$12,500 per academic year; it does not cover full costs, so applicants need other funding sources.

margaret-mcnamara-education-grants-2027.about:
Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG), founded in memory of Margaret McNamara by World Bank Group families, has supported 639 women from 81 countries. Its US-Canada Program gives grants to women from developing countries who are already enrolled full-time at accredited in-person universities in the United States or Canada, in fields such as engineering, IT, health, science, education, social studies and law.

Applicants must be at least 25 at the deadline, be nationals of a country on MMEG's eligibility list, hold a valid student visa, remain enrolled for at least one semester after the award and graduate within three years. Grantees commit to working in or with developing countries to improve the lives of women and/or children.

The US-Canada window runs from 15 September to 15 January (11:59 pm EST), with results in April. MMEG also runs programmes for students in France, South Africa and Latin America with their own windows. Essays must be your own; AI-written applications are disqualified.
highlights: For women 25+ from developing countries studying in the US or Canada
Grants go to students who will work to improve the lives of women and children
Deadline 15 January 2027
margaret-mcnamara-education-grants-2027.eligibility: Self-identifying women aged 25 or older at the deadline, nationals of countries on the MMEG eligibility list, enrolled full-time in an accredited in-person programme in the US or Canada with a valid student visa, staying enrolled at least one semester after the award and graduating within three years. Not US/Canadian citizens or permanent residents; relatives of World Bank Group, IMF or IDB staff are excluded.
how_to_apply: Read the eligibility criteria, checklist and FAQs on mmeg.org
Open the application portal and select 'US-Canada Program'
Upload every document on the checklist (incomplete applications are rejected)
Write your essays yourself and submit by 15 January 2027
margaret-mcnamara-education-grants-2027.costs: A one-time education grant; MMEG does not publish a fixed amount on its application page. It supplements other funding.

constructor-university-summer-camp-2027.about:
Constructor University (the former Jacobs University Bremen) is an English-speaking private research university in northern Germany. Its Talent School runs a 12-day international Summer Camp in which high-school students choose two of ten university-level courses: Mathematics & Modeling, Programming & Algorithms, AI & Robotics (building and training a robot with reinforcement learning), Chemistry & Research, Biology & Research, Physics & Research, Neuroscience & Psychology, Innovation & Entrepreneurship, Economics & Investments, and Probability & Data Science.

The 2027 camp runs 9–20 July 2027. Students live on the Bremen campus with mentors, mixing lectures, tutorials and team projects with sports, culture nights and excursions to Bremen and Hamburg. Past cohorts have included more than 40 nationalities.

The programme price of €5,100 includes tuition, accommodation, meals, excursions, domestic transport and supervision, with €500 off for applications before 31 December 2026. Flights, visa and health insurance are extra. It is a good way to test studying in Germany in English.
highlights: Choose 2 of 10 courses, including AI & Robotics and Data Science
All-inclusive price with campus housing and excursions
€500 early-bird discount until 31 December 2026
constructor-university-summer-camp-2027.eligibility: High-school students aged 16–18 from any country. Teaching is in English, so good English is needed.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 course list and choose two courses
Register on Constructor University's application portal, selecting Term 'Summer 2027' and Degree 'Summer Camp'
Complete and submit the application (see the programme FAQs for tips)
Apply before 31 December 2026 to get the €500 early-bird discount
After admission, pay and arrange your visa and insurance if needed
constructor-university-summer-camp-2027.costs: €5,100 for 2027 (€4,600 with early bird before 31 Dec 2026), including tuition, accommodation, meal plan, excursions and activities, domestic transport, mentoring and supervision. Not included: flights, visa fees, health insurance, pocket money. No scholarships advertised.

cern-particle-physics-course-high-school.about:
CERN's Particle Physics Course for High-School Students is a research-based online course created by CERN's Physics Education Research team. Its 16 chapters (about four hours in total) use short videos and self-grading quizzes to introduce fundamental questions such as 'What is a particle?', the Standard Model, the Higgs boson, the LHC and detectors such as ATLAS, antimatter, dark matter and dark energy, and how scientific inquiry works.

The course is free, self-paced and open all year to students aged 14–18 anywhere. Subtitles can be auto-translated into any language, and it includes do-it-yourself experiments and further reading. Students who complete all chapters and quizzes receive a digital certificate.

It is an ideal first step for students considering physics or engineering, and good preparation for CERN's Beamline for Schools competition. In September 2026 the course moved to the OpenLearn Create platform (previous learners must retake quizzes there).
highlights: Free, self-paced, about 4 hours
Digital certificate from CERN on completion
Subtitles auto-translated into any language
cern-particle-physics-course-high-school.eligibility: Designed for high-school students aged 14–18 worldwide; anyone can take it. No prerequisites.
how_to_apply: Open the course page on CERN's educational-resources site
Follow the link to the course on OpenLearn Create and create a free account
Work through the 16 chapters in order and complete each quiz
Download your digital certificate after finishing all chapters

smith-summer-science-engineering-program.about:
Established in 1990, Smith's Summer Science and Engineering Program (SSEP) is designed for high-school students with strong interests in science and engineering. Students take one lab-based course per two-week session with Smith faculty in the life sciences, physical sciences and engineering; recent courses include Designing Intelligent Robots and a sport and exercise psychology lab course. Those who stay both sessions take two courses.

The 2027 sessions are 3–16 July and 18–31 July. Students live on campus at Smith, one of the largest US women's colleges, and get a taste of college life with activities and weekend trips. College credit is not offered.

2026 tuition was US$4,985 per two-week session or US$9,970 for both (2027 rates coming soon). Need-based tuition assistance is available to a limited number of students (apply by 1 March 2027). International students must submit Duolingo, TOEFL or IELTS scores and apply by 1 March 2027.
highlights: Hands-on lab courses with Smith faculty, e.g. intelligent robots
One or two sessions to fit your summer
Need-based tuition assistance; international students welcome
smith-summer-science-engineering-program.eligibility: Students entering grades 9–12 in autumn 2027 with strong academic records; selection is based on grades, an essay and a teacher recommendation. Smith is a residential women's college: check the programme page for current eligibility. International students need an English test (Duolingo, TOEFL or IELTS) if not taught in English for more than two years.
how_to_apply: Open the application from 10 December 2026
Submit transcripts, the programme essay and a teacher recommendation
Apply by 1 February 2027 for priority review (decisions by 14 February)
International students and tuition-assistance applicants: submit by 1 March 2027, with tax documents if requesting aid
Pay the deposit after admission (US$1,246 per session in 2026)
smith-summer-science-engineering-program.costs: 2026 guide (2027 rates coming soon): US$4,985 per two-week session or US$9,970 for both, including room and board. Application fee rises to US$100 after 15 April 2027. Limited need-based tuition assistance.

harvard-cs50-scratch.about:
CS50's Introduction to Programming with Scratch is a free course from Harvard's CS50 team for absolute beginners, including younger students. Using Scratch, a visual block-based language from MIT, learners build animations, games and interactive stories while learning core ideas of programming: functions, conditionals, loops, variables and events.

Like other CS50 OpenCourseWare, it is free: watch the lectures, complete the problem sets and a final project, and receive a free CS50 certificate (a paid verified certificate is optional via edX).

It is an ideal first step before CS50x or CS50P, and a good recommendation for younger siblings or school coding clubs.
highlights: No experience needed; visual programming
Free CS50 certificate
Perfect bridge to CS50x
harvard-cs50-scratch.eligibility: Anyone; good for children and teenagers. Free edX account needed to submit work.
how_to_apply: Open cs50.harvard.edu/scratch.
Create a free Scratch account and an edX account as instructed.
Complete each problem set and the final project.
Claim your free CS50 certificate.
harvard-cs50-scratch.costs: Free; optional paid edX verified certificate.

ibm-skillsbuild.about:
IBM SkillsBuild offers 100% free learning in in-demand technology areas: artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data analytics, cloud, IT support and professional skills. It has separate sections for high-school students, university students and adult learners, with content available in more than 20 languages.

Courses are self-paced and range from short introductions to longer learning plans; completing them earns IBM-branded digital credentials (badges) that can be shared on LinkedIn or a CV. The university track includes project-based learning applying AI to real development tasks.

It is a credible, free way for students to explore tech careers and collect recognised badges before university.
highlights: 100% free; 20+ languages
Tracks for high school, university and adults
Shareable IBM digital credentials
ibm-skillsbuild.eligibility: Anyone; create a free account (age requirements per track).
how_to_apply: Go to skillsbuild.org and choose High school, University or Adult learners.
Sign up for a free account.
Pick a learning plan (e.g. AI fundamentals) and complete it.
Claim your digital credential.

college-board-sat-official-practice.about:
The College Board, which runs the SAT, provides free official preparation for the digital SAT. Its practice hub includes full-length practice tests taken in the Bluebook app (the same adaptive app used on test day, with scores and explanations), the Student Question Bank for targeted practice by skill and difficulty, a Study Plan Builder, Question of the Day, and guidance on how to use Khan Academy's free SAT practice.

Everything is free; you only need a College Board account. International students take the SAT at test centres worldwide, so practising in Bluebook is the best way to get used to the real interface.

For students applying to universities in the US and elsewhere that accept or require the SAT (see the university records on Meridian), official practice is the most reliable preparation available.
highlights: Full-length adaptive practice tests in Bluebook
Free Student Question Bank and study plan builder
Official guidance on Khan Academy practice
college-board-sat-official-practice.eligibility: Anyone preparing for the SAT; free College Board account.
how_to_apply: Create a free College Board account.
Download the Bluebook app and take a full-length practice test.
Review your score report and target weak skills in the Student Question Bank.
Use the Study Plan Builder and Khan Academy practice until test day.
college-board-sat-official-practice.costs: Free (the SAT exam itself is paid; fee waivers exist for eligible students).

ielts-official-preparation.about:
IELTS is jointly owned by the British Council, IDP and Cambridge University Press & Assessment, and is accepted by thousands of universities worldwide. Its official preparation hub gathers free resources: official sample questions and answers for Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking, videos explaining how the Writing test is scored, webinars, apps and links to teacher-led courses (some paid).

Using the official material helps you understand the exact format and band descriptors before you pay for the test, and to choose between IELTS Academic, General Training and IELTS for UKVI.

It is the right first step for any student who needs an English-language score for university applications or scholarships.
highlights: Official sample tests for all four skills
Videos on how Writing is scored
Free webinars and apps
how_to_apply: Open the IELTS preparation resources page.
Try the official sample tests for each section.
Watch the Writing scoring videos and study the band descriptors.
Book your IELTS Academic test when your practice scores meet your target.
ielts-official-preparation.costs: Preparation resources are free (some courses are paid; the test itself is paid).

un-sdg-learn.about:
UN SDG:Learn is a United Nations initiative that brings together learning offered by UN entities and partners on the Sustainable Development Goals. Learners can browse courses by SDG (from no poverty to partnerships for the goals) or by theme, and reach specialised community sites for statistics, evaluation, higher education and the Women2Lead initiative.

Courses are delivered on the providers' own platforms (for example UNITAR, UN CC:Learn, UNSSC and UN agencies); many are free and self-paced and award certificates of completion, while some professional courses are paid.

For students interested in MUN, international development or a UN career, it is the most direct way to find official UN training on any SDG.
highlights: Courses from UN entities in one catalogue
Browse by any of the 17 SDGs
Many free courses with certificates
un-sdg-learn.eligibility: Anyone; enrolment rules depend on each course provider.
how_to_apply: Go to unsdglearn.org and browse by SDG or theme.
Open a course and follow the link to the provider's platform.
Register (usually free) and complete the course.
Download the certificate where offered.
un-sdg-learn.costs: Many courses free; some professional courses paid.

amnesty-human-rights-academy.about:
Amnesty International's Human Rights Academy is a free online learning platform with self-paced courses on human rights. Courses range from introductions to human rights to specific themes and practical skills for taking action, and many are offered in several languages.

The Academy describes its courses as free, multilingual and certificated: you create a free account, complete a course at your own pace and download a certificate of completion. Check each course page for its length and available languages.

They are excellent preparation for human-rights MUN committees, debate topics and civic projects, and a meaningful certificate for youth activists.
highlights: Free courses with Amnesty certificates
Many languages
Short, self-paced modules
how_to_apply: Go to academy.amnesty.org and create a free account.
Choose a course and your language.
Complete the modules.
Download your certificate.

berkeley-math-tournament-online-2026.about:
The Berkeley Math Tournament (BMT) is run by students at the University of California, Berkeley, and describes itself as the largest student-run maths competition in the world. Its flagship in-person tournament is on 14 November 2026; BMT 2026 Online is the synchronous online version for students who cannot travel to California.

BMT 2026 Online has an asynchronous Power Round (a proof-based team round) on 28–29 November 2026 and a live event on 5 December 2026 with the Guts round and Focus/General rounds, featuring original problems. Teams have up to 6 students (teams of 1 are allowed, but 4+ is recommended); students do not need to be from the same school and can form teams without a coach, with a Teammate Finder available. It is open to all students in grade 12 and below; students outside the US can email the organisers about grade equivalency.

Registration is on ContestDojo until 27 November 2026 (USD 8 per student; fee waivers for financial hardship), and a parent/guardian must sign UC Berkeley's consent waiver. It is an accessible way for students anywhere to try a top US university maths tournament.

Teams of up to 6, formed across schools
USD 8 per student; fee waivers available
berkeley-math-tournament-online-2026.eligibility: Students in grade 12 or below anywhere in the world; must not have competed in another BMT 2026 iteration. Parent/guardian waiver required.
how_to_apply: Read the BMT 2026 Online event page on berkeley.mt.
Register on ContestDojo (as a coach or as students forming their own team) before 27 November 2026.
Have a parent/guardian sign the consent waiver in the portal.
Complete the Power Round on 28–29 November and the live rounds on 5 December 2026.
berkeley-math-tournament-online-2026.costs: USD 8 per student (fee waivers on request for financial hardship).

munov-2027.about:
Model United Nations of Vienna is run by students of the Vienna International School and is one of the few school MUNs that debates inside a real UN headquarters, the Vienna International Centre. The 2027 theme is 'Upholding and Safeguarding Rights & Information in an Increasingly Multi-polar World'.

The conference runs 20–22 January 2027 in Vienna, Austria at United Nations Office at Vienna (Vienna International Centre) and is aimed at high school students. Working language: English. Committees: General Assembly and specialised committees (list on the official committees page).

Schools and delegates register through the participation page; the site also offers a preparation centre, hotel and airline recommendations for visiting delegations. Delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions, which builds public speaking, research and negotiation skills valued by universities.

Warsaw Model United Nations is organised by students of the Stefan Batory High School and reaches its 20th edition in 2026. Its 18 committees include an EU Council, WTO, a historical committee and a crisis cabinet alongside classic UN bodies, and it is known for a friendly social programme in Warsaw.

The conference runs 12–15 November 2026 in Warsaw, Poland and is aimed at high school and university students. Working language: English. Committees: Security Council, Historical Committee, CSTD, CSW, HRC, UNEP, SPECPOL, Crisis, EU Council, ECOSOC, WTO and more (18 committees).

iliauni-georgian-as-a-foreign-language-a.about:
Ilia State University's Centre for Personal and Professional Development runs this A1 (beginner) course in Georgian as a foreign language for people who want to start from zero and adapt more easily to life in a Georgian-speaking environment. Teaching is based on modern conversational practice with many interactive activities.

The course covers everyday speaking (key phrases and expressions), reading and writing at beginner level (the Georgian alphabet, word order, understanding and writing simple texts), interactive practice through dialogues and role-plays, and cultural adaptation to Georgian daily life. It runs for 17 weeks (about 68 hours) from 26 November 2026: Mondays at 18:30 in person at the university with Professor Maia Damenia, an experienced teacher and textbook author in Georgian as a foreign language, and Thursdays at 18:30 online on Zoom with Maka Nozadze.

For international students coming to Tbilisi on exchange or for a degree, learning the alphabet and basic conversation early makes daily life, part-time work and friendships much easier, and a university-run course is more structured than apps or informal lessons.
highlights: Starts from the alphabet; no prior Georgian needed
Hybrid: 2 hours on campus + 2 hours on Zoom each week
Taught by Ilia State University faculty; 17 weeks
iliauni-georgian-as-a-foreign-language-a.eligibility: Anyone who wants to learn Georgian from beginner level, including foreign students, exchange students, expatriates and organisations (group registration possible). No prior knowledge of Georgian is required.
how_to_apply: Open the course page on the Ilia State University PPDC website
Complete the online registration form before 7 December 2026
Follow the payment guide (full fee or 200 GEL per month)
Join the first class on campus or on Zoom; questions to ppdc@iliauni.edu.ge
iliauni-georgian-as-a-foreign-language-a.costs: 800 GEL for the full course, payable in instalments of 200 GEL per month.

tsu-childrens-university-literary-odysse.about:
TSU Children's University is Tbilisi State University's long-running outreach programme (since 2007/08) that offers free educational projects to pupils from any public or private school. 'Literary Odyssey' is its new book club for teenagers aged 12 to 17, designed to develop critical thinking, close reading and a culture of discussion.

In the first season members read and discuss William Golding's Lord of the Flies, Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird, Jemal Karchkhadze's Antonio and David, Erich Maria Remarque's Three Comrades, Rabelais's Gargantua and Pantagruel and Ray Bradbury's Fahrenheit 451. Participants get three weeks to read each book, then meet at TSU for a group discussion of the author's intentions, characters' psychology and hidden symbols. The first meeting is on Wednesday 4 November 2026 at 16:00.

Selection is based on a short written task inside the registration form ('The main message of my favourite book'). It is a free, university-hosted way for literature-loving teens in Tbilisi to sharpen analytical writing and discussion skills that matter for essays and university applications.

Six classics in season 1, discussed every three weeks
Selection by a short essay on your favourite book
tsu-childrens-university-literary-odysse.eligibility: Pupils aged 12-17 from any public or private school. Discussions are in Georgian. Places are limited.

Fill in the registration form, including the short written task 'The main message of my favourite book'
Wait for selection results by email
Attend the first meeting on 4 November 2026 at 16:00; questions to junior@tsu.ge
tsu-childrens-university-literary-odysse.costs: Free. Participants buy or borrow the books themselves.

esc-info-session-ilia-state-university-n.about:
The European Solidarity Corps (ESC) is the EU programme that funds young people aged 18-30 to volunteer for two weeks to twelve months on social, environmental and educational projects across Europe and neighbouring countries, with travel, accommodation, food, insurance and pocket money covered. Georgia is a partner country, so young Georgians can take part.

On 6 November 2026 at 16:00 the youth organisation Umbrella will hold an information meeting in room G106 at Ilia State University (G. Tsereteli exit 1-3, Tbilisi). It covers short-term and long-term projects, funding conditions, what opportunities exist, how projects select volunteers and how to prepare a strong application.

For students who have heard of ESC but do not know where to start, a live session with an organisation that sends volunteers is the fastest way to understand the process and ask questions before applying to placements on the European Youth Portal.
highlights: Free, in person at Ilia State University, 6 Nov 2026
Explains short- and long-term funded volunteering in Europe
Practical tips on selection and applications
esc-info-session-ilia-state-university-n.eligibility: Open to anyone interested, especially young people aged 18-30 in Georgia who want to volunteer abroad. Session in Georgian. Pre-registration required.
how_to_apply: Open the announcement on the Ilia State University news page
Register in advance using the linked form
Attend on 6 November 2026 at 16:00 in room G106
Afterwards, create a profile on the European Solidarity Corps portal and apply to placements

ibsu-school-public-speaking-championship.about:
IBSU's Public Speaking Championship is a free project for pupils in grades 10, 11 and 12 who want to improve communication and presentation skills. It is run by the university's School of Law and Public Governance, with the dean among the trainers.

The programme helps participants build confidence, convey ideas clearly and persuasively, and run a speech effectively. Students learn to prepare logically structured, engaging talks, practise speaking in front of an audience and managing body language, and work on realistic scenarios before competing in a championship.

Strong spoken presentation helps in debate, Model UN, interviews and university admissions, and this is a free, structured way to practise it with university lecturers.

IBSU runs this free Mock Trial project for pupils in grades 11 and 12 who are interested in law and want practical experience of court proceedings.

Participants are introduced to the structure and stages of a trial, develop legal reasoning and critical thinking, practise legal argumentation and analysis of evidence, and then take part in a simulated court case under the guidance of IBSU law faculty.

For students considering law degrees in Georgia or abroad, it is a free, hands-on taste of legal practice that also builds the argument and public-speaking skills used in moot courts and debate.

postech-international-undergraduate-scho.about:
POSTECH in Pohang is a small, research-intensive science and technology university, one of Korea's leading institutions for science and engineering. International undergraduates are admitted twice a year through the International Admissions track (no interview required) and study alongside Korean students.

According to POSTECH's international admissions office, every admitted Korean and international undergraduate receives a full tuition waiver in the first semester; it continues for up to eight semesters for students who keep a GPA of at least 3.0/4.3. International students also receive a living allowance of KRW 500,000 per month (including vacations, no GPA requirement), an Arrival Scholarship reimbursing a one-way economy flight and domestic travel (up to KRW 2.5 million), a KRW 300,000 bonus for reaching TOPIK level 4, and from the fourth semester a Pathfinder learning voucher worth KRW 2.5 million a year. Scholarships are considered automatically during admission.

The Spring 2027 round has closed. The Fall 2027 intake is expected to open for applications from late March to early April 2027, with guidelines published in late January or early February 2027 and results in late June.

KRW 500,000/month living allowance for internationals
Flight to Korea reimbursed; no interview required
postech-international-undergraduate-scho.eligibility: Non-Korean international applicants (and eligible overseas Koreans) who have completed or will complete secondary school and meet POSTECH's academic and English requirements in the Fall 2027 guidelines.

Apply online during the late March – early April 2027 window

peking-university-international-student-.about:
Peking University (PKU) in Beijing is one of China's two most prestigious universities. In 2012 it created the Peking University International Student Scholarship to attract outstanding international students to its bachelor's, master's and doctoral programmes. For undergraduates it lasts four years and covers a tuition waiver, a living allowance and medical insurance, subject to passing an annual scholarship review.

Applicants must meet PKU's international admission requirements, have submitted an application to a full-time self-funded PKU degree programme, and hold no other scholarship. According to PKU's International Students Office, new bachelor's applicants do not need to submit a separate scholarship application: the university awards the scholarship on merit based on the final admission results. PKU admits international undergraduates through several routes, including an entrance examination, an exam-free route using recognised international test results, the Boya overseas talent programme and the Guanghua Future Leaders programme.

Scholarship applications at PKU generally take place between January and March each year; check the 2027 undergraduate admission brochure on the PKU International Students Office website as soon as it is published.

No separate application for new bachelor's students
Four years, renewed by annual review
